items.q: A patient says, “My father was diagnosed with colon cancer at age 46.” Which response by the nurse reflects the genomic guidance in the chapter?
items.a: “You will likely need a colonoscopy before age 45, and more often.”
items.ex: A relative with colon cancer before 50 signals risk, so family members need colonoscopy before 45 and more frequently.
w: “You can wait until age 60 for a colonoscopy, like most people.”
Family history before 50 means screening before 45, not waiting until 60.
“You need a colonoscopy only if symptoms appear after age 50.”
At-risk relatives need screening before 45, not only when symptomatic.
“Your risk is average, so routine screening at age 50 is enough.”
Family history of early colon cancer increases risk above average.

alt.q: A patient’s sister was diagnosed with colon cancer at age 42. What does this family history suggest for the patient?
alt.a: Increased risk, needing colonoscopy before age 45 and more frequently
alt.ex: When a family member has colon cancer before 50, relatives are likely at risk and need earlier, more frequent colonoscopy.
w: Average risk, needing colonoscopy only after age 60
Early-onset family history increases risk and calls for earlier screening.
Lower risk, because cancer before age 50 is not inherited
Early colon cancer in a relative suggests other family members are at risk.
No screening needed unless symptoms appear after age 50
At-risk relatives need screening before 45 regardless of symptoms.

items.q: Which actions are part of the nurse’s role in genomics and genetics-related care? Select all that apply.
o: Helping assess and interpret genomic test results
Nurses help assess and interpret genomic test results.
Identifying patients’ risk factors
Nurses identify patients’ risk factors.
Counseling patients about what a genomic finding means for them and their families
Nurses counsel patients about personal and family meaning of findings.
Sharing results with a patient’s employer to plan work duties
Genomic information must be used confidentially.
Disregarding cultural factors when discussing results
Genomic information must be used in a culturally appropriate manner.
items.ex: Nurses assess and interpret results, identify risk, and counsel patients, using genomic information confidentially, ethically, and in culturally appropriate ways.

alt.q: A nurse is discussing a patient’s genomic test results. Which practices are appropriate? Select all that apply.
o: Keeping the results confidential
Genomic information is used confidentially.
Discussing results in a culturally appropriate manner
Genomic information is used in a culturally appropriate manner.
Helping the patient and family make informed care decisions
Genomic information supports informed care decisions.
Posting the results where all unit staff can see them
Posting results violates confidentiality.
Telling the patient the results do not matter for relatives
Nurses counsel about what findings mean for families too.
alt.ex: Correct: Keeping the results confidential; Discussing results in a culturally appropriate manner; Helping the patient and family make informed care decisions.

items.q: Which statement about genomics and diseases such as cancer and heart disease is accurate?
items.a: They partly result from genes interacting with behaviors, environment, and social factors
items.ex: These diseases partly result from how genes interact with behaviors such as diet and activity, the environment, and social factors.
w: They result entirely from inherited genes, regardless of diet or activity
Behaviors, environment, and social factors also interact with genes.
They result only from behaviors such as diet, not from genetic factors
Genomics and family history play a role in these diseases.
They are unrelated to family health history or genomic changes
Family health history and genomics play a role in these diseases.

alt.q: A patient with a strong family history of heart disease says, “It’s in my genes, so nothing I do will matter.” Which response by the nurse is best?
alt.a: “Your genes interact with habits like diet and activity, which also affect risk.”
alt.ex: Disease risk partly reflects how genes interact with behaviors, environment, and social factors, so behaviors still matter.
w: “Because it is genetic, lifestyle changes will not affect your risk.”
Behaviors interact with genes and influence risk.
“Family history has little to do with heart disease risk.”
Family health history plays a role in heart disease.
“Only your environment, not your genes, determines your risk.”
Genes and environment both contribute to risk.

items.q: What is the purpose of the HCAHPS survey?
items.a: Measuring patients’ perspectives on hospital care in a standardized way
items.ex: HCAHPS is a standardized survey of patients’ perspectives on hospital care, allowing valid comparisons across hospitals.
w: Comparing hospitals’ clinical performance on specific diseases and procedures
This describes Hospital Compare.
Designating hospitals whose nursing leadership achieves excellence
This describes the Magnet Recognition Program.
Recording each patient’s orders and documentation electronically
This describes the EHR and CPOE.

alt.q: A consumer wants to directly compare several hospitals’ performance on heart failure and pneumonia care. Which resource should the nurse suggest?
alt.a: Hospital Compare
alt.ex: Hospital Compare lets consumers compare hospitals’ performance measures on specific diseases and procedures.
w: HCAHPS survey
HCAHPS compares patients’ perspectives on care, not disease-specific performance measures.
Electronic health record
The EHR documents an individual patient’s health information.
Computerized provider order entry
CPOE is a system for entering medical orders.

items.q: Nurses constitute the largest number of health care professionals.
items.a: True
items.ex: As frontline providers in all settings, nurses make up the largest number of health care professionals.
items.ww: The chapter states nurses constitute the largest number of health care professionals.

alt.q: Nurses practice mainly in hospitals and are not considered frontline providers in other health care settings.
alt.a: False
alt.ex: Nurses are frontline health care providers who practice in all health care settings.
alt.ww: The chapter describes nurses as frontline providers in all settings, not only hospitals.

items.q: Which is a purpose of the American Nurses Association described in the chapter?
items.a: Improving health standards and access to health care services for all people
items.ex: The ANA works to improve health standards and service availability, foster high standards, promote development, and advance nurses’ welfare.
w: Issuing state nursing licenses to new graduates
Licensure is not described as an ANA purpose.
Restricting its services according to nationality or creed
ANA purposes are unrestricted by nationality, race, creed, or other factors.
Setting hospital prices for health care services
Setting prices is not described as an ANA purpose.

alt.q: A nurse joins the ANA to support professional development. Which additional ANA purpose is described in the chapter?
alt.a: Advancing nurses’ economic and general welfare
alt.ex: Among its purposes, the ANA advances nurses’ economic and general welfare.
w: Accrediting hospitals for Medicare payment
Hospital accreditation is not described as an ANA purpose.
Limiting membership by race or gender
ANA purposes are unrestricted by race, gender, or other factors.
Prescribing treatments for nurses’ patients
Prescribing is not an ANA purpose.

items.q: A nurse wants to influence health policy decisions that affect patients in the community. Which action is most effective, according to the chapter?
items.a: Becoming involved early in local and national policy efforts
items.ex: Involvement in local and national efforts early in the political process is critical to expanding nurses’ influence.
w: Waiting until legislation passes before offering an opinion
Influence depends on involvement early in the political process.
Leaving policy work entirely to hospital administrators
Every nurse can influence policy by participating in efforts.
Limiting advocacy to individual patients at the bedside
Nurses also advocate through involvement in public policy.

alt.q: According to the chapter, what happens as nurses become involved in public policy?
alt.a: They grow more aware of social needs and influence policy to meet them
alt.ex: Through policy involvement, nurses become aware of social needs and active in influencing policy to meet those needs.
w: They withdraw from professional nursing organizations
Involved nurses are generous contributors to nursing organizations.
They focus less on universal access to good health care
Involved nurses support candidates working for universal good health care.
They lose influence early in the political process
Early involvement is how nurses expand their influence.

items.q: Professional nursing organizations and State Boards of Nursing employ [[lobbyists]] to urge legislatures and Congress to pass laws that improve the quality of health care.
items.ex: Lobbyists employed by nursing organizations and boards urge legislators to pass laws improving health care quality.

alt.q: To persuade state legislatures and the U.S. Congress to pass legislation improving health care quality, nursing organizations hire [[lobbyists]].
alt.ex: Lobbyists employed by nursing organizations and boards urge legislators to pass laws improving health care quality.

items.q: What do graduates of associate degree and bachelor’s degree nursing programs have in common?
items.a: Both are eligible to take the NCLEX-RN to become licensed
items.ex: Associate and bachelor’s degree programs are the most frequent routes to RN licensure, and both lead to NCLEX-RN eligibility.
w: Both programs require 4 years of college study
The associate degree program is a 2-year program; only the bachelor’s program usually takes 4 years.
Both include required courses in the arts and humanities
Social sciences, arts, and humanities are added in the bachelor’s program, not the associate program.
Both qualify the graduate to practice as an APRN
A master’s degree is the minimum requirement for an APRN.

alt.q: Which statement about the most common routes to RN licensure in the United States is accurate?
alt.a: Associate and bachelor’s graduates both qualify to sit for the NCLEX-RN
alt.ex: Graduates of both associate and bachelor’s programs are eligible for the NCLEX-RN in the state where they will practice.
w: Only bachelor’s graduates may sit for the NCLEX-RN
Associate degree graduates are also eligible to take the NCLEX-RN.
Associate graduates take a different licensing exam
All RN candidates take the NCLEX-RN regardless of educational preparation.
Associate graduates must finish a BSN before testing
An associate degree alone makes a graduate eligible for the NCLEX-RN; the BSN can be earned later.

items.q: Which description fits the associate degree nursing program in the United States?
items.a: A 2-year program at a university or community college focused on basic sciences and nursing courses
items.ex: The associate program lasts 2 years and covers basic sciences plus theoretical and clinical nursing courses.
w: A 4-year university program that adds social sciences, arts, and humanities courses
This describes the bachelor’s degree program.
A 12- to 18-month program that builds on an existing associate degree RN license
This describes an RN-to-BSN program for nurses who already hold an associate degree.
A graduate program that prepares nurses for educator and advanced practice roles
Graduate (master’s or doctoral) education prepares nurses for these roles.

alt.q: Which feature distinguishes the bachelor’s degree program from the associate degree program?
alt.a: Added courses in the social sciences, arts, and humanities
alt.ex: The bachelor’s program adds social sciences, arts, and humanities to support nursing theory.
w: Courses in anatomy, physiology, and other basic sciences
Both associate and bachelor’s programs focus on the basic sciences.
Theoretical and clinical courses in nursing practice
Both programs include theoretical and clinical nursing courses.
Eligibility to sit for the NCLEX-RN licensing exam
Graduates of both programs are eligible to take the NCLEX-RN.

items.q: An RN with an associate degree asks the nurse educator how long an RN-to-BSN program will take. Which response is most accurate?
items.a: About 12 to 18 months, depending on your associate degree transcript
items.ex: Each university sets the added coursework, so RN-BSN programs take 12 to 18 months based on the student’s transcript.
w: Exactly 2 years, because every program requires identical courses
Each university determines its own additional coursework, so length varies.
A full 4 years, because associate credits do not transfer to a BSN
The associate degree transcript is used, so the program is far shorter than 4 years.
About 6 months, because the RN license replaces most BSN coursework
The textbook cites 12 to 18 months, not 6 months.

alt.q: Which factor determines the additional coursework an associate degree RN needs to earn a BSN?
alt.a: The individual university, based on the student’s transcript
alt.ex: Each university determines the added coursework, which depends on the student’s associate degree transcript.
w: The State Board of Nursing in the nurse’s state
State boards oversee the nurse practice act, not RN-BSN coursework.
The nurse’s score on the NCLEX-RN examination
NCLEX-RN results grant licensure; they do not set BSN coursework.
A single national RN-BSN curriculum set by the ANA
No single national curriculum exists; each university sets its own coursework.

items.q: What is the main purpose of The Essentials: Core Competencies for Professional Nursing Education?
items.a: To guide faculty on the structure and evaluation of nursing curricula
items.ex: The AACN Essentials outline domains that guide how nursing curricula are structured and evaluated.
w: To set the passing standard for the NCLEX-RN
The Essentials address education, not the licensure examination.
To define each state’s legal scope of nursing practice
Each state’s nurse practice act defines the legal scope of practice.
To grant Magnet designation to health care organizations
Magnet designation comes from the American Nurses Credentialing Center.

alt.q: How many domains for the baccalaureate-prepared nurse are included in the AACN Essentials (2021)?
alt.ex: The AACN Essentials contain 10 domains, from Knowledge for Nursing Practice to Personal, Professional, and Leadership Development.
w: Six is the number of ANA Standards of Practice, not AACN domains.
There are 10 domains; Domains 9 and 10 cover professionalism and leadership development.
Eighteen is the total count of ANA standards of practice and performance, not AACN domains.

w: 2-year program focused on basic sciences and nursing theory and clinical courses

Bachelor of Science in Nursing

alt.a: Doctor of Nursing Practice

items.q: Which are AACN Essential Domains for professional nursing education? Select all that apply.
o: Person-Centered Care
Person-Centered Care is Domain 2 of the AACN Essentials.
Population Health
Population Health is Domain 3 of the AACN Essentials.
Quality and Safety
Quality and Safety is Domain 5 of the AACN Essentials.
Informatics and Healthcare Technologies
Informatics and Healthcare Technologies is Domain 8 of the AACN Essentials.
Resource Stewardship
Resource Stewardship is an ANA Standard of Professional Performance, not an AACN domain.
Environmental Health
Environmental Health is an ANA Standard of Professional Performance, not an AACN domain.
items.ex: The AACN Essentials list 10 domains that guide curriculum; they differ from the ANA standards of practice and performance.

alt.q: Which domains appear in the AACN Essentials (2021)? Select all that apply.
o: Interprofessional Partnerships
Interprofessional Partnerships is Domain 6.
Systems-Based Practice
Systems-Based Practice is Domain 7.
Scholarship for the Nursing Discipline
Scholarship for the Nursing Discipline is Domain 4.
Professionalism
Professionalism is Domain 9.
Coordination of Care
Coordination of Care is ANA Standard of Practice 5a, not an AACN domain.
Outcomes Identification
Outcomes Identification is ANA Standard of Practice 3, not an AACN domain.
alt.ex: Correct: Interprofessional Partnerships; Systems-Based Practice; Scholarship for the Nursing Discipline; Professionalism.

items.q: The Institute of Medicine recommended that 80% of nurses be prepared with a bachelor’s degree in nursing by 2020.
items.a: True
items.ex: The IOM’s recommendation set an 80% target for BSN-prepared nurses by 2020.
items.ww: The textbook cites this IOM recommendation directly as an 80% BSN target.

alt.q: The Institute of Medicine recommended that half of all nurses hold a bachelor’s degree in nursing by 2020.
alt.a: False
alt.ex: The IOM target was 80% of nurses with a BSN by 2020, not 50%.
alt.ww: Half understates the recommendation; the IOM called for 80% BSN-prepared nurses.

items.q: A master’s degree in nursing is the minimum educational requirement for which role?
items.a: Advanced practice registered nurse
items.ex: A master’s degree is a minimum requirement for an APRN and is important for educator, administrator, and researcher roles.
w: Registered nurse
An RN can be licensed after an associate or bachelor’s degree program.
Nurse manager
Nurse manager positions usually require at least a bachelor’s degree.
Staff RN in a critical care unit
Specialty units require experience plus continuing or in-service education, not a master’s degree.

alt.q: A nursing student with an associate degree says, “I plan to become a nurse practitioner as soon as I pass the NCLEX-RN.” Which response by the nurse is best?
alt.a: “An APRN role requires at least a master’s degree, so you will need more education first.”
alt.ex: Nurse practitioners are APRNs, and a master’s degree is the minimum requirement for an APRN.
w: “Passing the NCLEX-RN qualifies you to practice as a nurse practitioner.”
The NCLEX-RN licenses an RN; APRN practice requires graduate education.
“You only need a specialty certification after you are licensed.”
Certification alone does not replace the graduate degree an APRN needs.
“A bachelor’s degree is the minimum for nurse practitioners.”
A BSN is not enough; a master’s degree is the APRN minimum.

items.q: Which doctoral degree is the terminal practice degree that provides advanced preparation for APRNs?
items.a: Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP)
items.ex: The DNP is a practice-focused doctorate and the terminal practice degree for APRNs.
w: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in nursing
The PhD is research-oriented, preparing nurses for rigorous research and theory development.
Doctor of Nursing Science (DNSc)
The DNSc prepares graduates to apply research findings to clinical nursing.
Master of Science in Nursing (MSN)
A master’s degree is not a doctorate; it is the APRN minimum, not the terminal degree.

alt.q: A nurse wants a doctoral degree focused on rigorous research and theory development. Which program best fits this goal?
alt.a: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in nursing
alt.ex: The research-oriented PhD prepares nurses for rigorous research and theory development.
w: Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP)
The DNP is practice-focused, preparing APRNs rather than researchers.
Doctor of Nursing Science (DNSc)
The DNSc focuses on applying research findings to clinical nursing.
Master of Science in Nursing (MSN)
The MSN is not a doctoral degree.

items.q: The Doctor of Nursing Science (DNSc) degree prepares graduates to apply research findings to clinical nursing.
items.a: True
items.ex: Professional doctoral programs (DSN or DNSc) prepare graduates to apply research findings to clinical nursing.
items.ww: Applying research findings to clinical nursing is exactly how the textbook describes DSN/DNSc preparation.

alt.q: The Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) is a research-oriented doctorate designed mainly for theory development.
alt.a: False
alt.ex: The DNP is a practice-focused doctorate; the PhD is the research-oriented degree.
alt.ww: Research and theory development describe the PhD, not the DNP.

items.q: Which reasons does the textbook give for the increasing need for doctoral-prepared nurses? Select all that apply.
o: Expanding clinical roles
Expanding clinical roles call for more doctoral-prepared nurses.
Continuing demand for well-educated nursing faculty
Demand for well-educated faculty drives the need for doctoral nurses.
Demand for nurse administrators and APRNs in clinical settings
Administrators and APRNs in clinical settings are cited as reasons.
New specialty areas such as nursing informatics
New specialties such as informatics increase the need for doctoral nurses.
A shrinking need for bachelor’s-prepared bedside nurses
The textbook supports more BSN-prepared nurses, not fewer.
Elimination of the NCLEX-RN for doctoral graduates
All RN candidates must pass the NCLEX-RN regardless of education.
items.ex: Expanding roles, faculty and administrator demand, APRN needs, and new specialties like informatics increase the need for doctoral nurses.

alt.q: A nurse asks why so many doctoral-prepared nurses are needed. Which reasons are supported by the textbook? Select all that apply.
o: Need for well-educated nursing faculty
Continuing demand for faculty is one reason cited.
Growth of new specialties such as nursing informatics
Informatics is named as a new specialty needing doctoral nurses.
Demand for APRNs in clinical settings
APRNs in clinical settings are part of the growing demand.
A rule that all staff nurses must hold a doctorate
Staff RNs may be prepared with associate or bachelor’s degrees.
Replacement of the master’s degree as the APRN minimum
The textbook states a master’s degree remains a minimum requirement for an APRN.
alt.ex: Correct: Need for well-educated nursing faculty; Growth of new specialties such as nursing informatics; Demand for APRNs in clinical settings.

items.q: Which statement best describes the purpose of continuing education for nurses?
items.a: It updates knowledge of current research and practice and teaches new skills
items.ex: Continuing education updates knowledge, helps nurses specialize, and teaches new skills and techniques to improve care.
w: It provides the initial education needed to sit for the NCLEX-RN
Prelicensure associate or bachelor’s programs provide this education.
It is training an agency gives only to its own employees on-site
This describes in-service education.
It replaces the need for an RN license in a specialty area
Continuing education supports practice; it never replaces licensure.

alt.q: Which program is an example of continuing education rather than in-service education?
alt.a: A university program on caring for older adults with dementia
alt.ex: Continuing education is offered by universities, hospitals, associations, and organizations, such as a university program on dementia care.
w: A hospital session for its staff on new safety syringes
Agency training on new technology for its own staff is in-service education.
A hospital’s required staff training on chemotherapy safety
Training to meet an agency’s required competencies is in-service education.
A unit training for its employees on a new infusion pump
Agency training for employees on new equipment is in-service education.

items.q: A hospital is introducing a new model of safety syringe and needs its nurses to use it correctly. Which type of education is most appropriate?
items.a: An in-service program held at the hospital for its employees
items.ex: In-service programs are held in the institution for its employees and often focus on new technologies such as safety syringes.
w: A university-based continuing education course
A university course is not tailored to this agency’s new equipment and staff.
A Doctor of Nursing Practice degree program
A DNP is advanced graduate preparation, not equipment training.
A specialty certification examination
Certification recognizes expertise in a specialty, not use of new equipment.

alt.q: Which characteristic defines in-service education?
alt.a: It is provided by an agency for its own employees within the institution
alt.ex: In-service education is training held in the institution to build the knowledge and skills of its own staff.
w: It must be taken at a university for academic credit
University-based programs describe academic or continuing education.
It leads to specialty certification from a national group
Certification follows set practice or education requirements and an exam.
It is offered only by state nurses’ associations
State nurses’ associations are among continuing education providers, not in-service.

items.q: A nurse is preparing to renew a state RN license. Which action is most appropriate?
items.a: Check the state’s required continuing education hours and topics
items.ex: Many states require a set number of continuing education hours, sometimes on specific topics, for license renewal.
w: Retake the NCLEX-RN to demonstrate current competence
The NCLEX-RN is taken for initial licensure, not renewal.
Complete a graduate degree before the renewal date
A graduate degree is not required to renew an RN license.
Obtain a specialty certification, which every renewal requires
Certification is a voluntary choice after licensure, not a renewal requirement.

alt.q: Which topics does the textbook give as examples of specific continuing education requirements for license renewal?
alt.a: Bioterrorism and pain management
alt.ex: Some states require continuing education on specific topics such as bioterrorism and pain management.
w: Chemotherapy safety and safety syringes
These are examples of in-service program topics.
Epidemiology and public health
These are graduate fields a BSN-prepared nurse may pursue.
Advanced cardiac life support and trauma
These are certifications often required of ICU and emergency nurses.

items.q: A nurse in a rural clinic needs oncology continuing education, but the nearest university is hours away. Which suggestion best fits the textbook?
items.a: Look for a virtual learning or mobile simulation oncology program
items.ex: Virtual learning and mobile simulation are growing to serve subspecialties such as oncology and nurses in rural areas.
w: Wait until an on-site oncology lecture is offered locally
Waiting delays needed learning when virtual options exist.
Substitute a general in-service on new unit equipment
An equipment in-service does not meet oncology subspecialty education needs.
Rely on informal advice from experienced co-workers instead
Informal advice isn't continuing education; virtual and mobile programs bring formal education to rural nurses.

alt.q: Why are virtual learning and mobile simulation growing in continuing nursing education?
alt.a: They serve nursing subspecialties and nurses in rural areas
alt.ex: These formats meet the needs of subspecialties like oncology and nurses in rural areas.
w: They are the only format accepted for license renewal
Many programs are still lectures, seminars, or skills labs.
They replace the need for clinical practice hours
Clinical practice hours are still needed, for example to maintain certification.
They are required for new graduates before the NCLEX-RN
Continuing education occurs after licensure, not before the NCLEX-RN.

items.q: Which does the textbook list as providers of continuing education for nurses? Select all that apply.
o: Universities
Universities offer continuing education, such as a program on dementia care.
Hospitals
Hospitals offer continuing education, such as safe medication practices.
State nurses’ associations
State nurses’ associations are listed as providers.
Professional nursing organizations
Professional nursing organizations are listed as providers.
State nurse practice acts
An NPA is a law regulating scope of practice, not an education provider.
The NCLEX-RN testing program
The NCLEX-RN is a licensure exam, not a continuing education provider.
items.ex: Continuing education comes from universities, hospitals, state nurses’ associations, professional organizations, and educational and health care institutions.

alt.q: Which are benefits of continuing education described in the textbook? Select all that apply.
o: Updates knowledge about the latest research and practice
Keeping current is a key purpose of continuing education.
Helps the nurse specialize in an area of practice
Continuing education supports specialization.
Teaches new skills and techniques
Learning new skills and techniques improves patient care.
Replaces the need for license renewal
Continuing education is often required for renewal; it does not replace it.
Qualifies the nurse to practice as an APRN
APRN practice requires graduate education and certification.
alt.ex: Correct: Updates knowledge about the latest research and practice; Helps the nurse specialize in an area of practice; Teaches new skills and techniques.

items.q: In-service education programs are often designed to fulfill an organization’s required competencies.
items.a: True
items.ex: Many in-service programs meet required competencies, such as safe chemotherapy administration.
items.ww: The textbook states that many in-service programs fulfill an organization’s required competencies.

alt.q: In-service education programs are designed only to help nurses earn an advanced academic degree.
alt.a: False
alt.ex: In-service programs are offered by the employer to build job competencies, such as using new safety syringes; they don't award degrees.
alt.ww: Calling it true confuses in-service education with graduate education, which leads to a degree.

items.q: Training provided by a health care agency for its own employees and held within the institution is called [[in-service education|in-service|inservice education|in-service program]].
items.ex: In-service programs build the knowledge, skills, and competencies of an institution’s own employees.

alt.q: A hospital program on safe chemotherapy administration for its own nurses is an example of [[in-service education|in-service|inservice education|in-service program]].
alt.ex: In-service programs build the knowledge, skills, and competencies of an institution’s own employees.

items.q: Which statement about entry into nursing practice is accurate according to the textbook?
items.a: Standardizing education for entry into practice remains a major controversy
items.ex: Standardization of nursing education and entry into practice remains controversial, which can make choosing a program hard.
w: A bachelor’s degree is now required for new RNs in every state
Associate degree graduates remain eligible for the NCLEX-RN and licensure.
Associate degree graduates are licensed only as practical nurses
Associate degree graduates are eligible for RN licensure through the NCLEX-RN.
Entry into practice was standardized nationally by the IOM
The IOM made a recommendation; entry into practice is still debated.

alt.q: Why can choosing a prelicensure nursing program sometimes be difficult?
alt.a: Standardization of education and entry into practice is still debated
alt.ex: Ongoing controversy over standardization and entry into practice can make choosing a program difficult.
w: Only bachelor’s programs lead to RN licensure
Both associate and bachelor’s graduates can become RNs.
Each state requires a different licensing exam
All states require the same NCLEX-RN.
Associate degree programs no longer exist
The associate degree is one of the most frequent routes to RN licensure.

items.q: A nurse educated in Canada holds a Bachelor in Nursing (BN). How does this degree compare with U.S. preparation?
items.a: It is equivalent to a U.S. Bachelor of Science in Nursing
items.ex: In Canada, the BScN or BN is equivalent to the BSN in the United States.
w: It is equivalent to a U.S. associate degree in nursing
The BN is a bachelor’s-level degree, not a 2-year associate degree.
It is equivalent to a U.S. master’s degree in nursing
The BN is undergraduate, not graduate, preparation.
It is equivalent to a U.S. Doctor of Nursing Practice
The DNP is a terminal practice doctorate, far beyond a bachelor’s.

alt.q: In Canada, which degrees are equivalent to the U.S. BSN?
alt.a: BScN or BN
alt.ex: The Canadian BScN or BN degree is equivalent to the U.S. BSN.
w: ADN or ASN
These are associate-level degrees, not equivalents of the BSN.
MSN or MN
These are master’s-level graduate degrees.
DNP or DNSc
These are doctoral degrees.

items.q: Who oversees the nurse practice act in each U.S. state?
items.a: The State Board of Nursing
items.ex: In the United States, each State Board of Nursing oversees its nurse practice act.
w: The American Nurses Association
The ANA develops professional standards, not state law.
The American Association of Colleges of Nursing
The AACN publishes education Essentials, not state regulations.
The International Council of Nurses
The ICN offers a global definition of nursing, not state oversight.

alt.q: Which establishes the specific legal regulations for nursing practice?
alt.a: State and provincial nurse practice acts
alt.ex: NPAs establish legal regulations; professional organizations set standards of practice as criteria for care.
w: ANA Standards of Professional Performance
These are professional criteria for competent behavior, not legal regulations.
Specialty nursing organizations
Specialty organizations improve standards and roles but do not make law.
The nursing code of ethics
The code is a statement of philosophical ideals, not legal regulation.

items.q: What is the primary purpose of a state’s nurse practice act?
items.a: To regulate the scope of nursing practice and protect the public
items.ex: The NPA regulates scope of practice and protects public health, safety, and welfare, including from unqualified and unsafe nurses.
w: To set salary and benefit levels for nurses in the state
NPAs regulate practice, not pay.
To certify nurses in specialties such as geriatric nursing
National organizations such as the ANA offer specialty certification.
To define philosophical ideals of right and wrong for nurses
That is the role of the nursing code of ethics.

alt.q: A nursing student asks why the state has a nurse practice act. Which response by the instructor is best?
alt.a: “It defines your legal scope of practice and protects the public from unsafe nurses.”
alt.ex: The NPA regulates scope of practice and protects the public from unqualified and unsafe nurses.
w: “It lists the ethical ideals you must adopt instead of your own values.”
The code of ethics states ideals, and nurses also incorporate their own values.
“It sets the curriculum that every nursing school must teach.”
Curricula are guided by the AACN Essentials and accrediting standards.
“It keeps your employer from assigning tasks outside your specialty.”
NPAs define legal scope of nursing, not employer assignments by specialty.

items.q: Each state has its own nurse practice act, but most NPAs are similar.
items.a: True
items.ex: States write their own NPAs, yet most are similar, and the ANA definition represents most states’ scope.
items.ww: The textbook says that although each state has its own NPA, most NPAs are similar.

alt.q: The ANA definition of nursing practice is the binding legal definition in every state.
alt.a: False
alt.ex: The ANA definition is representative of most states, but each state’s NPA is the legal authority.
alt.ww: Legal scope comes from each state’s NPA; the ANA definition is a professional statement.

items.q: Many states have revised their nurse practice acts during the last decade. Which changes do these revisions reflect? Select all that apply.
o: Growing autonomy of nursing
Revisions reflect nursing’s growing autonomy.
Minimum education requirements
Revisions address minimum education requirements.
Certification requirements
Revisions address certification requirements.
Expanded roles and scope of practice of APRNs
Revisions reflect the expanded roles of APRNs.
Elimination of the NCLEX-RN for BSN graduates
All state boards still require the NCLEX-RN regardless of education.
Removal of criminal background checks
Background checks remain a licensure requirement that varies by state.
items.ex: NPA revisions reflect growing autonomy, minimum education and certification requirements, and expanded APRN roles.

alt.q: Which topics have states addressed when revising nurse practice acts in recent years? Select all that apply.
o: Expanded scope of practice of APRNs
APRN roles and scope are a major focus of revisions.
Certification requirements
Certification requirements are included in revisions.
Minimum education requirements
Minimum education requirements are included in revisions.
Nurse salary scales
NPAs regulate practice, not salaries.
Hospital Magnet designation criteria
Magnet designation is granted by the ANCC, not set by NPAs.
alt.ex: Correct: Expanded scope of practice of APRNs; Certification requirements; Minimum education requirements.

items.q: A new graduate of an associate degree program asks whether BSN graduates take a different licensing exam. Which response by the nurse is accurate?
items.a: “All RN candidates take the NCLEX-RN, regardless of educational preparation.”
items.ex: Every state board of nursing requires RN candidates to pass the NCLEX-RN regardless of educational preparation.
w: “BSN graduates take a more advanced version of the NCLEX-RN.”
There is one NCLEX-RN for all RN candidates.

items.q: Which list correctly names the six traditional levels of care in the U.S. health care system?

items.ex: The book names six levels of care: preventive, primary, secondary, tertiary, restorative, and continuing.
w: Primary, secondary, tertiary, acute, chronic, and hospice
Acute, chronic, and hospice are not levels; preventive, restorative, and continuing care are missing.
Preventive, primary, acute, critical, rehabilitative, and palliative
Critical and palliative are not levels; secondary, tertiary, restorative, and continuing care are the correct names.
Promotion, prevention, diagnosis, curing, managing, and restoring
These words describe prevention activities and goals, not the six levels of care.

w: Secondary, primary, and preventive care
Intensive care is tertiary, rehabilitation is restorative, and assisted living is continuing care.
Tertiary, secondary, and primary care
Rehabilitation programs are restorative and assisted living is continuing care, not secondary or primary.
Secondary, tertiary, and preventive care
Intensive care is tertiary, and neither rehabilitation nor assisted living is preventive care.

items.q: A nurse in a primary care clinic sees a patient with long-standing asthma for a routine visit. Which nursing focus best reflects the nurse’s role at this level of care?

w: Begin teaching now so the plan stays on schedule

alt.q: Why should a nurse delay discharge teaching for a patient who is confused and in severe pain?

alt.ww: Hospice is not for patients still pursuing cure; it begins when all agree treatment will not reverse the disease.

Hospice is for the terminal phase of illness, which is not described here.

All nurses are expected to participate fully in health care change.

Technology helps, but the book names nurses’ participation as key.
The decisions of health insurance companies
Insurers are partners in cost control, not the main source of solutions.

Priorities favor telehealth and in-home services over inpatient expansion.

items.q: A hospital adopts value-based care, one of the post-pandemic priorities. Which nursing action best supports this priority?

w: Increasing the number of tests ordered for each patient
Extra testing raises costs without improving quality.
Delaying discharge teaching until the day the patient leaves
Teaching should start early; late teaching risks poor outcomes and readmission.
Focusing on speed of tasks over clear communication
Clear communication affects satisfaction, a quality measure tied to payment.

alt.q: Under value-based care, how are hospital payments affected?
alt.a: Payments are tied to quality outcomes such as readmissions
alt.ex: Pay-for-value programs link payment to quality measures, including readmissions and hospital-acquired conditions.
w: Payments rise with the number of services provided
Paying more for more services is not value-based care.
Payments equal whatever the hospital chooses to charge
Governmental programs and DRGs set payment amounts.
Payments are unaffected by patient satisfaction scores
Patient satisfaction measures are linked to hospital reimbursement.

items.src: Ch 2 · The health care delivery system

items.q: A patient living in a remote rural area has trouble arranging transportation to follow-up appointments. Which benefit of expanding telehealth applies most directly?
items.a: Reducing patient costs by eliminating the need to travel
items.ex: Telehealth reduces patient costs by removing the need to travel, take time off, or arrange family caregiving.
w: Replacing the need for any future in-person care
Telehealth increases access but does not replace all in-person care.
Eliminating privacy concerns about health information
Privacy remains a concern with digital tools.
Removing the need for the nurse’s clinical judgment
Technology never replaces the nurse’s clinical judgment.

alt.q: Which statement about telehealth is accurate?
alt.a: It uses interactive video when patient and provider are in different places
alt.ex: Telehealth relies on interactive video conferencing when patient and provider are not in the same place.
w: It requires the patient and provider to be in the same room
Telehealth is used when they are not in the same place.
It is limited to hospitals and cannot reach patients’ homes
Information can be gathered at a home, clinic, or other site.
It increases patient costs because of added travel
Telehealth reduces costs by eliminating travel.

Equity focuses on removing barriers, not identical treatment.
Making all persons feel welcomed and respected in a setting
This describes inclusion.
The many characteristics that make up individuals
This describes diversity.

items.src: Ch 2 · The health care delivery system

items.q: The three primary drivers of change in health care are technology, [[consumerism]], and the unsustainable cost structure of health care.
items.ex: Consumerism, along with technology and cost, is pushing health care to place the consumer at the center.

alt.q: Along with technology and consumerism, the unsustainable [[cost structure|cost|costs|cost structure of health care]] of health care is a primary driver of change.
alt.ex: Consumerism, along with technology and cost, is pushing health care to place the consumer at the center.

items.src: Ch 2 · The health care delivery system

items.q: Health care organizations are implementing new and improved technologies. What do the book’s stated aims of these technologies include? Select all that apply.
o: Reducing unnecessary costs
New technologies aim to reduce unnecessary costs.
Improving access to care
New technologies aim to improve access to care.
Improving the quality of patient care
New technologies aim to improve quality of care.
Replacing the nurse’s clinical judgment
Technology never replaces a nurse’s clinical judgment.
Shifting the focus of care from patient to device
The focus of nursing care is the patient, not the machine.
items.ex: Organizations adopt technology to change how services are provided, reduce unnecessary costs, and improve access and quality.

alt.q: A nurse is evaluating a new technology for the unit. Which criteria reflect the book’s guidance? Select all that apply.
o: It improves the effectiveness of nursing care
Nurses should use technology that improves care effectiveness.
It enhances patient safety
Nurses should use technology that enhances safety.
It improves patient outcomes
Nurses should use technology that improves outcomes.
It allows nurses to spend less time connecting with patients
Nurses must stay connected with patients and preserve their dignity.
It removes the need to monitor patients directly
Nurses must still monitor and use clinical judgment.
alt.ex: Correct: It improves the effectiveness of nursing care; It enhances patient safety; It improves patient outcomes.

items.src: Ch 2 · The health care delivery system

items.q: Which statement best describes the goals future health care systems must meet while controlling costs?
items.a: Care that is safe, high quality, accessible, and affordable for all
items.ex: Future systems must control costs while providing safe, quality care that is accessible and affordable for all.
w: Care that is fast, specialized, hospital based, and fully private
The book emphasizes access and affordability, not hospital-based or private care.
Care that is low cost even if quality and safety decline
Cost control must not sacrifice safe, quality care.
Care that is high tech, insurer directed, and provider centered
The future model is consumer centered, not insurer or provider centered.

alt.q: A policy committee is setting goals for a future health system. Which goal reflects the book’s description?
alt.a: Control costs while keeping care safe, high quality, and affordable
alt.ex: The book calls for cost control combined with safe, quality, accessible, and affordable care for all.
w: Control costs by limiting care to insured patients
Care must be accessible and affordable for all.
Increase spending without regard to sustainability
The current cost structure is already unsustainable.
Improve quality by ending all telehealth programs
Telehealth is expected to grow and is a priority to expand.

items.src: Ch 2 · The health care delivery system

items.q: A patient says, “I want to choose when and how I get care, like booking visits and seeing results on my phone.” Which driver of health care change does this best illustrate?
items.a: Consumerism
items.ex: Consumerism is a primary driver of change, pushing the future model to place the consumer at the center.
w: Nursing shortage
The nursing shortage is a workforce issue, not a consumer expectation.
Unsustainable costs
Cost is a driver, but this statement reflects consumer expectations.
Population aging
Aging is not one of the three primary drivers the book names.

alt.q: Which trend reflects consumerism as a driver of health care change?
alt.a: Patients expecting care designed around their needs and choices
alt.ex: Consumerism places the consumer at the center of the future health care model.
w: Hospitals setting care schedules to suit staff
This is provider centered, not consumer driven.
Insurers deciding which hospital patients must use
This reflects payer control, not consumer choice.
Providers making care decisions without patient input
Consumer-centered care requires patient involvement.

items.src: Ch 2 · The health care delivery system

items.q: The COVID-19 pandemic uncovered priorities intended to make future health care more accessible, more affordable, and focused on what?
items.a: Preventive health
items.ex: The pandemic revealed priorities that could make care more accessible and affordable and focused on preventive health.
w: Inpatient surgery
The priorities favor in-home and telehealth services, not inpatient surgery.
Specialist referral
The priorities emphasize prevention and integrated systems, not specialist referral.
Emergency care
The book names preventive health, not emergency care, as the focus.

alt.q: During the COVID-19 pandemic, many people with chronic illnesses delayed seeking care. How does this relate to the future priority of focusing on improving health?
alt.a: Delays worsened health, showing the need for preventive, accessible care
alt.ex: Delayed care led to exacerbations and worse health, supporting a future focus on preventive and accessible care.
w: Delays improved health, showing that most visits are unnecessary
Delayed care caused exacerbations and worsening overall health.
Delays had no effect, showing that acute care is sufficient
Waiting until symptoms develop makes care more expensive and health worse.
Delays reduced costs, showing that preventive care is too expensive
Acute care after delay is costly; prevention reduces overall costs.

items.src: Ch 2 · The health care delivery system

items.q: A patient going home after a cardiac event will use a smart watch that transmits heart data to the clinic. Which statement by the patient shows understanding of this technology?
items.a: “My care team can monitor my data remotely, and I can check my status too.”
items.ex: Wearables let patients monitor their own status and transmit data remotely for monitoring by health care professionals.
w: “The watch will treat any heart problem automatically.”
Wearables monitor and transmit data; they do not treat conditions.
“Now I won’t need any follow-up with my health care team.”
Wearable data supports, rather than replaces, follow-up by professionals.
“Only the clinic can see my data, so I can’t use it myself.”
Wearables allow patients to monitor their own status as well.

alt.q: Which description of wearable technology in telemedicine is accurate?
alt.a: It lets patients track their status and send data to professionals
alt.ex: Wearable technology, such as a smart watch, supports self-monitoring and remote monitoring by health care professionals.
w: It is used only inside hospitals and cannot transmit data
Wearables transmit data remotely from outside the hospital.
It replaces the need for telehealth video visits entirely
Wearables are one expanding component of telemedicine, not a replacement for it.
It can be used only by health care professionals
Patients use wearables to monitor their own status.

items.src: Ch 2 · The health care delivery system

items.q: Which statement best describes the focus of community-based health care?
items.a: It emphasizes primary care and reaches everyone in a community, including the underinsured
items.ex: Community-based health care reaches all community members, including the poor and underinsured, and focuses on primary rather than institutional or acute care.
w: It emphasizes acute care delivered mainly within hospital-based institutions
Community-based care occurs outside traditional institutions and focuses on primary rather than acute care.
It serves mainly insured patients referred by hospital-based specialists
It reaches everyone in the community, including the poor and underinsured.
It focuses on rehabilitation of individuals after inpatient discharge
Its focus is primary care, health promotion knowledge, and models of care for the whole community.

alt.q: A nursing student says, “Community-based health care means caring for people in hospitals near their homes.” Which reply by the instructor is most accurate?
alt.a: It takes place outside hospitals, in settings such as clinics, schools, and places of worship
alt.ex: Community-based health care occurs outside traditional institutions, in nontraditional settings such as ambulatory clinics, senior centers, places of worship, and schools.
w: It takes place in hospitals, as long as they are located in the community
Community-based care occurs outside traditional health care institutions such as hospitals.
It takes place only in patients’ homes through home health agencies
Settings include ambulatory clinics, hospice centers, senior centers, places of worship, and schools, not only homes.
It takes place mainly in specialty acute care units that serve rural areas
It focuses on primary rather than acute care and occurs outside institutions.

items.q: A family without a regular health care provider needs blood pressure checks for an older relative. Which setting is an example of community-based health care?
items.a: A senior center offering weekly health screenings
items.ex: Senior centers are nontraditional community settings where people unable to access care elsewhere can receive services.
w: A hospital’s cardiac intensive care unit
Intensive care is institutional acute care, not community-based care.
An inpatient medical-surgical nursing unit
Inpatient units are traditional institutional settings, not community-based ones.
A hospital-based surgical recovery room
A recovery room is part of a hospital, a traditional institution.

alt.q: Why is community-based care offered in nontraditional settings such as schools and places of worship?
alt.a: They reach people unable to access care in other areas
alt.ex: Nontraditional settings let people who cannot access care elsewhere receive needed care, decreasing vulnerability in at-risk populations.
w: They allow complex acute procedures to be done at lower cost
Community-based care focuses on primary rather than acute care.
They replace the need for hospitals in urban communities
Community services are provided within, not instead of, existing health care services.
They are required by law for publicly insured patients
The reason given is improved access for people unable to get care elsewhere, not a legal requirement.

items.q: Which factor does the textbook identify as influencing public health problems and health care services today?
items.a: Social determinants of health
items.ex: Political policy, social determinants of health, increasing health disparities, and economics all influence public health problems and services.
w: Overimmunization of infants and children
The problem identified is underimmunization of infants and children.
Declining rates of sexually transmitted infections
The text notes an increase, not a decline, in sexually transmitted infections.
Falling rates of chronic illnesses such as diabetes
Chronic illnesses such as heart disease and diabetes are listed as ongoing problems.

alt.q: Which is a public health problem the textbook lists as a current challenge for community-based health care?
alt.a: Underimmunization of infants and children
alt.ex: Listed problems include inadequate insurance, chronic illness, substance abuse, rising sexually transmitted infections, and underimmunization of infants and children.
w: Excess hospital bed capacity in rural areas
This is not a listed problem; some rural communities lack acute care agencies altogether.
Decreasing incidence of sexually transmitted infections
The text describes an increase, not a decrease, in sexually transmitted infections.
Overuse of preventive screening by adolescents
Overuse of screening is not identified as a public health problem in the text.

items.q: What is the goal of population health?
items.a: To improve health equity and the health of all people
items.ex: Population health spans public health prevention through population disease management, with the goal of improving health equity and everyone’s health.
w: To reduce hospital costs by shortening inpatient stays
Cost reduction in hospitals is not the stated goal of population health.
To manage acute illness in hospitalized patients
Population health covers prevention through disease management across populations, not acute inpatient care.
To provide specialty care to insured groups only
Population health seeks equity and better health for all people, not only insured groups.

alt.q: Which description of population health is accurate?
alt.a: A continuum from public health prevention through population disease management
alt.ex: Population health covers the care delivery continuum from public health prevention through population disease management, including community partnerships.
w: A care model limited to acute treatment delivered in hospitals
Population health begins with public health prevention and is not limited to acute care.
A program that serves only individuals with chronic disease
Population health addresses all people, aiming to improve health equity.
A form of private insurance that covers entire communities
Population health is a delivery continuum, not an insurance product.

items.q: Healthy People goals for the U.S. population are updated every 10 years based on program evaluation data and national health trends.
items.a: True
items.ex: Healthy People tracks the nation’s health and updates its goals every 10 years using evaluation data and national trends.
items.ww: The update cycle is 10 years, so the statement is accurate.

alt.q: Healthy People goals are revised every 5 years based on hospital discharge data.
alt.a: False
alt.ex: Goals are updated every 10 years using data from program evaluation and national health trends.
alt.ww: No 5-year cycle is described; the interval is 10 years and data come from program evaluation and national trends.

items.q: Which are overall goals of Healthy People 2030? Select all that apply.
o: Increase life expectancy and quality of life
This is one of the overall Healthy People 2030 goals.
Attain health literacy
Attaining health literacy is an overall Healthy People 2030 goal.
Achieve health equity
Achieving health equity is an overall Healthy People 2030 goal.
Eliminate health disparities
Eliminating health disparities through improved care delivery is an overall goal.
Increase the number of hospital beds nationwide
Expanding hospital capacity is not a Healthy People 2030 goal.
Shift resources from prevention to acute treatment
Healthy People emphasizes health promotion and prevention, not a shift to acute care.
items.ex: Healthy People 2030 aims to increase life expectancy and quality of life, attain health literacy, achieve health equity, and eliminate disparities.

alt.q: A nurse is explaining Healthy People 2030 at a community meeting. Which goals should the nurse include? Select all that apply.
o: Eliminating health disparities
Eliminating health disparities is an overall Healthy People 2030 goal.
Improving health literacy across the population
Attaining health literacy is an overall goal.
Increasing life expectancy and quality of life
This is an overall Healthy People 2030 goal.
Reducing the number of community health programs
Healthy People supports, rather than reduces, community health programs.
Limiting public health services to insured citizens
Healthy People seeks health equity and access for all members of the population.
alt.ex: Correct: Eliminating health disparities; Improving health literacy across the population; Increasing life expectancy and quality of life.

items.q: What is the first component of improved health care delivery described in the textbook?
items.a: Assessing the health care needs of individuals, families, and communities
items.ex: Assessment, including systematic data collection and monitoring health status, is the first component; policy and access to care follow.
w: Developing public policies that support a population’s health
Policy is the second component and is driven by assessment data.
Ensuring access to essential community-wide health services
Access to care is the last of the three components.
Evaluating outcomes of the national health program
Evaluation is not named as one of the three components.

alt.q: Which three components does improved health care delivery involve?
alt.a: Assessment, policy development, and access to care
alt.ex: Improved health care delivery involves assessment, development and implementation of public health policies, and improved access to care.
w: Diagnosis, treatment, and rehabilitation
These describe individual medical care, not the three delivery components.
Screening, referral, and hospital admission
These are individual care activities, not the components of improved delivery.
Funding, staffing, and accreditation
These are administrative concerns, not the three components named in the text.

items.q: A community health nurse is concerned about motor vehicle crashes involving teenage drivers. Which action should the nurse take first?
items.a: Gather data on the number of crashes caused by teen drivers
items.ex: Assessment comes first; documenting crashes caused by teen drivers informs programs to reduce distractions for teen drivers.
w: Start a distracted-driving program at the local high school
Program development should follow and be informed by a community assessment.
Lobby the city council for stricter teen driving laws
Strong policies are driven by assessment data, which must be gathered first.
Refer all teen drivers in the area to a safety course
Intervening before assessing skips the first component, assessment of needs.

alt.q: A nurse plans an adolescent sex education program for a community. Which information should the nurse gather first?
alt.a: The community’s adolescent pregnancy rates
alt.ex: Determining adolescent pregnancy rates is community assessment data that informs adolescent sex education programs.
w: The costs of hospital labor and delivery units
Hospital costs do not describe the adolescent health need the program addresses.
The number of private obstetricians in nearby cities
Provider counts in other cities do not assess this community’s adolescent needs.
The number of hospital beds in the region
Bed counts are not relevant to planning an adolescent education program.

items.q: Assessment shows high blood lead levels among young children in a city. Which nursing action reflects the policy component of improved health care delivery?
items.a: Lobbying for a lead cleanup program and educating families about exposure
items.ex: In Flint, Michigan, nurses lobbied for and educated families about lead exposure, a policy effort driven by assessment data.
w: Documenting each child’s lead level in the health record
Recording data is part of assessment, not policy development.
Drawing blood samples from children for lead screening
Screening children is data collection, part of the assessment component.
Treating children with lead poisoning in the hospital
Inpatient treatment is acute care, not public policy work.

alt.q: Which statement about public health policy is accurate according to the textbook?
alt.a: Strong policies are driven by community assessment
alt.ex: Health professionals lead policy development, and strong policies grow out of community assessment data.
w: Policies should be written before community data are collected
Assessment comes first; strong policies are driven by assessment data.
Nurses have little role in developing public health policy
Nurses can lead policy efforts, such as lead cleanup and opioid prescription monitoring.
Policy development is the last component of improved delivery
Policy is the second component; access to care is the last.

items.q: Which factors are essential in establishing access to community-wide health promotion and health maintenance activities? Select all that apply.
o: Insurance coverage
Insurance coverage is named as essential to establishing access.
Geographic availability of care
Care must be geographically available for community members to use it.
Relationships with health care providers
Developing relationships with providers is essential to access.
Admission to a specialty hospital unit
Hospital admission is acute care, not a basis for community-wide access.
Referral by a private physician for every service
Access aims to make services available to all, not only those with private referrals.
items.ex: Insurance coverage, geographic availability of care, and relationships with health care providers are essential to community-wide access.

alt.q: A nurse evaluates whether a neighborhood has adequate access to care. Which factors should the nurse consider? Select all that apply.
o: Whether residents have insurance coverage
Insurance coverage is an essential part of access to care.
Whether care is available within reasonable distance
Geographic availability of care is essential to access.
Whether residents have relationships with providers
Relationships with health care providers support access to health promotion services.
Whether residents can see a hospital-based specialist
Specialist access is not among the essential access factors named in the text.
Whether the neighborhood has a trauma center
Trauma centers provide acute care; access here concerns community-wide health promotion and maintenance.
alt.ex: Correct: Whether residents have insurance coverage; Whether care is available within reasonable distance; Whether residents have relationships with providers.

items.q: Which description defines social determinants of health?

Systematic collection of data to monitor a community’s overall health status

alt.q: A nurse notes that a family lives in unsafe housing in a neighborhood with polluted air. These conditions are best described as which of the following?

Health resources go first to people with insurance coverage
Equity applies to all people regardless of factors that affect access to care.

Equity concerns fair opportunity, not identical disease rates.

items.q: Which statement by a nursing student shows understanding of health disparities?
items.a: They stem from many factors, such as poverty, environmental threats, and poor access to care
items.ex: Health disparities are multifactorial, including poverty, environmental threats, inadequate access, behavioral factors, and educational inequalities.
w: They are unavoidable differences caused only by genetic factors
Health disparities are preventable and have many contributing factors.
They affect only people who live in rural geographic areas
Geography is one of many characteristics; others include race, income, gender, and disability.
They result mainly from individual choices about diet and exercise
Individual behaviors are one factor among many, including poverty and access to care.

alt.q: A nurse reviews county data showing that one ethnic group has much higher infant mortality than others. How should the nurse interpret this finding?
alt.a: A health disparity exists because outcomes vary by population
alt.ex: A disparity exists when health outcomes vary by population; such differences are preventable and call for action.
w: Health equity has been achieved because services exist
Unequal outcomes show equity has not been achieved.
The difference is expected and needs no intervention
Health disparities are preventable differences that should be addressed.

items.q: Health disparities usually result from a single cause, most often a lack of health insurance.

items.ex: Health disparities are multifactorial: poverty, environmental threats, inadequate access, individual and behavioral factors, and educational inequalities.
items.ww: Lack of insurance can contribute, but disparities have many causes, not one.

alt.q: Cognitive, sensory, or physical disability can contribute to health disparities.

alt.ex: The text lists cognitive, sensory, or physical disability among characteristics contributing to health disparities.

items.q: What is the goal of community health nursing?
items.a: To preserve, protect, promote, or maintain health within a community
items.ex: Community health nursing improves the health of individuals, families, and groups, aiming to preserve, protect, promote, or maintain community health.
w: To provide acute care to individuals after hospital discharge
Acute post-discharge care is not the stated goal of community health nursing.
To replace primary care providers in underserved areas
Community health nurses work with, not instead of, primary care providers.
To manage hospital admissions for high-risk families
The goal centers on community health, not hospital admissions.

alt.q: Which statement best describes the focus of community health nursing?

alt.ex: Community health nursing focuses on improving the health care of individuals, families, and groups within their communities.
w: Providing intensive care to individuals in specialty hospital units
Intensive care is institutional acute care, not community health nursing.

Financial management is not the focus of community health nursing.
Treating acute illness in patients transferred from rural hospitals
Treating transferred acute patients is hospital-based care.

items.q: A [[population]] is a collection of individuals who have one or more personal or environmental characteristics in common.

alt.q: Public health nursing requires understanding the needs of a [[population]], such as high-risk infants, older adults, or an ethnic group.
alt.ex: Public health nursing requires understanding the needs of a population, a group sharing personal or environmental characteristics.

items.ex: Populations share personal or environmental characteristics; examples include high-risk infants, older adults, or an ethnic group such as Native Americans.
w: A single patient admitted for pneumonia
One patient is an individual, not a collection of individuals.
One family receiving a home visit
A single family is one unit, not a population.
A nurse’s list of unrelated appointments
These people share no defined personal or environmental characteristic.

alt.q: Which feature defines a population?
alt.a: Members share one or more personal or environmental characteristics
alt.ex: A population is a collection of individuals who have one or more personal or environmental characteristics in common.
w: Members must be related by blood or marriage
Relationship by blood or marriage describes a family, not a population.
Members must number at least several thousand people
No minimum size is part of the definition.
Members must all be hospitalized at the same time
Populations live in communities; hospitalization is not a defining feature.

items.q: Which areas does a public health nurse need to understand? Select all that apply.
o: Factors that influence health promotion and health maintenance
Public health nurses understand factors that influence health promotion and maintenance.
Trends and patterns in the incidence of disease within populations
Understanding disease trends and patterns within populations is required.
Environmental factors that contribute to health and illness
Environmental contributors to health and illness are part of this knowledge.
Political processes that affect public policy
Public health nurses understand political processes that shape public policy.
Billing codes for inpatient surgical procedures
Inpatient billing is not part of public health nursing knowledge.
Advanced surgical techniques used in acute care
Surgical techniques belong to acute care, not population-focused practice.
items.ex: Public health nurses understand health promotion factors, disease trends within populations, environmental factors, and political processes affecting policy.

alt.q: A public health nurse is preparing to address rising rates of a disease in a city. Which knowledge areas apply to this work? Select all that apply.
o: Patterns of disease incidence within the population
Trends and patterns of disease incidence guide population-focused work.
Environmental factors contributing to illness
Environmental factors contributing to health and illness are part of public health knowledge.
Political processes that shape public policy
Policy change is a tool public health nurses use, so political processes matter.
Operating room scheduling procedures
Operating room scheduling is unrelated to population health work.
Inpatient medication cart management
This is a hospital unit task, not population-focused knowledge.
alt.ex: Correct: Patterns of disease incidence within the population; Environmental factors contributing to illness; Political processes that shape public policy.

items.q: A public health nurse notes an increase in playground injuries in the city. Which action best reflects population-focused public health nursing?
items.a: Lobbying for shock-absorbing surfaces instead of concrete in new playgrounds
items.ex: Using injury data to change public policy protects the whole population of children, which is the focus of public health nursing.
w: Applying first aid to each child injured at a playground
This is individual care and does not prevent injuries across the population.
Telling parents to keep children away from all playgrounds
This does not address the environmental cause of injuries.
Referring each injured child to an orthopedic specialist
Referrals treat individuals after injury rather than preventing injuries.

alt.q: Why does a public health nurse need to understand the political processes that affect public policy?
alt.a: Policy change can address a health problem across a whole population
alt.ex: Public health nurses use data and policy, such as safer playground surfaces, to improve the health of entire populations.
w: To run for public office as part of the nursing role
Holding office is not part of the public health nursing role described.
To determine individual patients’ insurance eligibility
Insurance eligibility is not the purpose of understanding policy processes.
To decide which hospital units receive funding
Hospital funding decisions are not the focus of public health nursing.

items.q: A community health nurse case manager follows several older adults recovering from stroke and notices that many lack rehabilitation after discharge. Which action best reflects community health nursing?
items.a: Identifying the need for community rehabilitation services for this group
items.ex: The case manager sees the subpopulation’s need for community rehabilitation services, caring for the community rather than one person.
w: Recommending that each patient be readmitted for therapy
Readmission is an individual, hospital-based response, not a community service.
Focusing only on the patient with the most severe deficits
Focusing on one patient ignores the group at risk.
Telling families that recovery depends on patient effort
This dismisses the unmet need rather than addressing it.

alt.q: A nurse practitioner in a community clinic screens patients for sexually transmitted infections. What is the population-level purpose of this activity?
alt.a: Preventing the spread of communicable disease in the community
alt.ex: Screening a subpopulation for sexually transmitted infections prevents communicable diseases from spreading within the community.
w: Reducing the clinic’s cost of laboratory testing
Screening is done to prevent disease spread, not to cut costs.
Meeting requirements for hospital admission
Screening is not linked to hospital admission requirements.
Diagnosing chronic illnesses in older adults
The purpose described is preventing communicable disease, not chronic illness diagnosis.

items.q: By focusing on subpopulations, a community health nurse considers an individual or family as only one member of a group at risk.
items.a: True
items.ex: Focusing on subpopulations lets the nurse care for the community, viewing each individual or family as one member of an at-risk group.
items.ww: The statement matches the text; the community, through the at-risk group, is the focus of care.

alt.q: When caring for a subpopulation, a community health nurse treats each family as an isolated client separate from the larger group at risk.
alt.a: False
alt.ex: The nurse considers each family only one member of a group at risk, caring for the community as a whole.
alt.ww: Families are not treated as isolated clients; they are viewed as part of the at-risk group.

items.q: According to the ANA position statement, which educational preparation is required for entry-level public health nursing roles?

w: An associate degree in nursing (ADN)
The ANA position requires a baccalaureate, not an associate degree, for public health entry roles.
A master’s degree in public health (MPH)
A graduate degree is not required for entry-level public health nursing.
A doctorate in nursing practice (DNP)

alt.q: A new graduate with an associate degree asks about entry-level public health nursing positions. Which information from the nurse mentor is accurate?
alt.a: Public health nursing requires a baccalaureate degree in nursing

w: Any registered nurse license qualifies for public health roles
Licensure alone is not enough; the BSN is required for entry-level roles.
A graduate degree is the minimum for any public health role
The entry-level requirement is the baccalaureate, not a graduate degree.
Public health certification replaces the need for a degree
No certification is described as replacing the BSN requirement.

items.q: A nurse with a graduate nursing degree who practices in a community setting is considered a community health nurse specialist only after gaining public health experience.
items.a: False
items.ex: Graduate-prepared nurses who practice in community settings are community health nurse specialists regardless of public health experience.
items.ww: Public health experience is not required for the specialist designation.

alt.q: Educational requirements for entry-level community health nursing roles vary by practice setting and location.
alt.a: True
alt.ex: The text states entry-level educational requirements for community health nursing roles vary by setting and location.
alt.ww: Unlike public health nursing’s BSN requirement, community health entry requirements are not uniform.

items.q: Competence as a community health nurse requires the ability to use which kind of interventions?

items.ex: Community health nursing competence requires interventions that take in the broad social and political context of the community.
w: Interventions limited to direct bedside care of individuals
Competence extends beyond individual bedside care to the community context.
Interventions focused solely on hospital discharge teaching
Discharge teaching alone does not address the community’s social and political context.
Interventions that avoid involvement in public policy matters
Community health nurses engage with political processes that affect policy.

alt.q: Which nurse demonstrates competence in community health nursing?
alt.a: One who plans interventions within the community’s social and political context
alt.ex: Competent community health nurses use interventions that include the broad social and political context of the community.
w: One who restricts care to individual physical assessments
Individual assessments alone do not reflect the community context.
One who avoids working with local government officials
Engaging political processes is part of community health competence.
One who addresses only the problems families raise at visits
Competence includes the broader community context, not only reported problems.

items.q: Only nurses with advanced degrees can formulate and apply population-focused assessments and interventions.
items.a: False
items.ex: Experts usually have advanced degrees, but the baccalaureate-prepared nurse generalist can also formulate and apply population-focused assessments and interventions.
items.ww: The text explicitly includes BSN generalists in this work.

alt.q: Nurses who become experts in community health practice usually have advanced nursing degrees.
alt.a: True
alt.ex: Expert community health nurses usually hold advanced nursing degrees, though BSN generalists also perform population-focused work.
alt.ww: The text states experts usually have advanced degrees, so the statement is accurate.

items.q: In community health nursing, clinical judgment about how best to partner with families involves applying which areas of knowledge? Select all that apply.

Public health principles are part of this clinical judgment.
