Family theory guides how the nurse partners with families.
Communication principles
Communication principles are applied in partnering with families.
Critical thinking
Critical thinking is applied to choose the best approaches.
Hospital reimbursement rules
Reimbursement rules are not listed as part of this clinical judgment.
Intraoperative nursing techniques
Operating room skills are not relevant to partnering with families in the community.
items.ex: Clinical judgment applies public health principles, community health nursing, family theory, communication principles, and critical thinking to partnering with families.

alt.q: A community health nurse is deciding how to partner with a family facing barriers to care. Which knowledge should guide this decision? Select all that apply.
o: Community health nursing knowledge
Community health nursing knowledge is part of this clinical judgment.
Public health principles

Surgical asepsis procedures

items.q: A community health nurse notices that more grandparents in the community are assuming child care responsibilities. Which action best demonstrates successful community health nursing practice?

items.ex: Successful practice responds to community changes; the nurse partners with schools to support grandparents in the caregiving role.
w: Referring each grandparent to a hospital parenting class
Hospital referrals are individual and do not build community partnerships.
Waiting until a grandparent asks for help before acting
Successful practice is responsive to community changes, not passive.
Advising parents to hire professional child care instead
This ignores the community’s actual situation and needs.

alt.q: What makes community health nursing practice successful, according to the textbook?
alt.a: Building relationships with the community and responding to its changes
alt.ex: Successful practice involves building community relationships and being responsive to changes within the community.
w: Following a fixed program regardless of community changes
Practice must be responsive to changes within the community.
Working independently from community leaders and schools
Nurses collaborate with community leaders to build effective programs.
Focusing on the acute care needs of individual patients
The focus is community health promotion and disease prevention.

items.q: When establishing health promotion programs, a community health nurse often works with resistant systems. What are these systems?
items.a: Health and human service systems
items.ex: The nurse works with resistant health and human service systems, encouraging them to respond better to a population’s needs.
w: Family systems led by older relatives
Family systems are not the resistant systems described in the text.
Local school administration systems
Schools are partners in the example, not the resistant systems named.
Hospital information technology systems
IT systems are not the resistant systems the text describes.

alt.q: What is the nurse’s aim when working with resistant health and human service systems?
alt.a: Encouraging them to be more responsive to a population’s needs
alt.ex: The nurse tries to encourage resistant systems to be more responsive to the needs of a population.
w: Replacing them with new nurse-run agencies
Nurses design new systems in cooperation with existing ones, not replacements.
Avoiding them and serving families directly
The nurse works with these systems rather than avoiding them.
Reporting them to state regulators for closure
The aim is responsiveness, not closure.

items.q: Which skills help make community nursing practice effective? Select all that apply.
o: Patient advocacy
Patient advocacy is named as a skill that makes practice effective.
Communicating people’s concerns
Communicating community members’ concerns supports effective practice.
Designing new systems in cooperation with existing systems
Cooperative system design is named as an effective skill.
Replacing existing systems without community input
New systems are designed in cooperation with existing systems.
Making health decisions on behalf of community members
Nurses advocate and communicate concerns; they do not decide for the community.
items.ex: Skills in patient advocacy, communicating people’s concerns, and designing new systems in cooperation with existing systems make community nursing effective.

alt.q: A community health nurse is working to improve a population’s access to services. Which approaches reflect effective community nursing practice? Select all that apply.
o: Advocating for patients within health and human service systems
Patient advocacy is an effective community nursing skill.
Voicing community members’ concerns to decision makers
Communicating people’s concerns makes practice effective.
Designing new systems that cooperate with existing ones
New systems should be designed in cooperation with existing systems.
Bypassing existing systems to create separate services
Effective practice works in cooperation with existing systems.
Limiting contact to individual patients at clinic visits
Effective practice involves the broader community, not only clinic visits.
alt.ex: Correct: Advocating for patients within health and human service systems; Voicing community members’ concerns to decision makers; Designing new systems that cooperate with existing ones.

items.q: How does an expert community health nurse come to understand a population’s needs?

items.ex: Experts understand population needs through experience with families or populations, including working through social and health care barriers.
w: By reviewing national statistics without contact with families
Understanding comes through direct experience with families and populations.
By completing a graduate degree, regardless of practice experience
A degree confers a title; understanding needs comes through experience.
Through hospital practice caring for acutely ill patients
Acute hospital care does not build understanding of community needs.

alt.q: Which experience best prepares a community health nurse to understand a community’s needs?
alt.a: Working with families through social and health care barriers to care
alt.ex: Experience with families and populations, including working through social and health care barriers, builds understanding of community needs.
w: Rotating through hospital critical care units
Critical care experience does not build understanding of community needs.
Studying the community from published reports alone

Supervising staff in a long-term care facility
Facility supervision is not the experience described for community experts.

items.q: A nursing student is assigned to a community health nurse who follows families with high-risk infants. Which statement by the student shows understanding of community health nursing?
items.a: “This family is one member of a larger group at risk in the community.”
items.ex: Community health nurses consider an individual or family as only one member of an at-risk group within the community.
w: “This family is my only client, so the community is not my concern.”
The community, not a single family, is the focus of care.
“Our goal is to treat the infant’s acute illness during the visit.”
The goal is to preserve, protect, promote, or maintain community health.
“Population data are not useful when visiting a single family.”
Population trends and patterns guide care of at-risk groups.

alt.q: Which statement by a nurse reflects a population-focused perspective?
alt.a: “I use trends in disease incidence to plan care for at-risk groups.”
alt.ex: Public health nurses understand trends and patterns in disease incidence and use them to care for populations.
w: “I focus only on what each patient tells me during the visit.”
This is individual focus, not population focus.
“I leave public policy decisions entirely to elected officials.”
Public health nurses understand and influence political processes and policy.
“I plan each patient’s care without regard to community trends.”
Population-focused care uses community trends to plan care.

items.q: Why does a community health nurse collaborate with community leaders?
items.a: To establish effective health promotion and disease prevention programs
items.ex: Knowing members’ needs and resources, the nurse collaborates with leaders to establish effective health promotion and disease prevention programs.
w: To obtain funding for hospital expansion projects
Hospital expansion is not the purpose of this collaboration.
To transfer responsibility for patient care to them
The nurse partners with leaders but keeps a nursing role.
To enforce health regulations on community families
Collaboration aims at building programs, not enforcement.

alt.q: A community health nurse wants to start a disease prevention program. Which action best supports success?
alt.a: Learning community members’ needs and resources and partnering with leaders
alt.ex: Effective programs come from knowing community members’ needs and resources and collaborating with community leaders.
w: Designing the program alone using hospital protocols
Programs succeed through collaboration with the community, not in isolation.
Copying a program from another state without changes
Programs should reflect this community’s own needs and resources.
Waiting for health systems to request the program
The nurse actively encourages resistant systems to respond to needs.

items.q: A baccalaureate-prepared nurse generalist at a county health department notices that many older adults in one neighborhood cannot reach the clinic. Which action is within this nurse’s role, according to the textbook?
items.a: Conducting a population-focused assessment and planning interventions
items.ex: BSN-prepared generalists can formulate and apply population-focused assessments and interventions.
w: Waiting for an advanced practice nurse to assess the group
Population-focused assessment is not limited to advanced practice nurses.
Referring the issue to the hospital emergency department
An emergency department does not address a community access problem.
Limiting care to older adults who manage to reach the clinic
This ignores the at-risk group the nurse has identified.

alt.q: A nurse identifies that a neighborhood’s older adults cannot reach the clinic. Which intervention is population focused?
alt.a: Working with community partners to provide transportation for the group
alt.ex: Population-focused interventions address the whole at-risk group, often by working with community partners and systems.
w: Rescheduling one older adult’s missed appointment
This helps one individual, not the group.
Teaching one patient to read a bus schedule
This is individual teaching, not a population intervention.
Documenting each missed visit in the health record
Documentation does not change access for the group.

items.q: Which description best fits community-based nursing care?
items.a: Care in homes, clinics, or outpatient centers focused on an individual’s or family’s needs
items.ex: Community-based nursing occurs in settings such as homes, clinics, or outpatient centers, focusing on individual and family needs.
w: Care in acute care hospitals focused on a single body system
Community-based nursing takes place outside acute care hospitals.
Policy work aimed at the health needs of a whole nation
Community-based nursing centers on individuals and families in local settings.
Care in long-term psychiatric institutions for chronic illness
This is institutional care, not community-based nursing.

alt.q: Which goal is part of community-based nursing care?
alt.a: Enhancing patients’ capacity for self-care and autonomy in decision making
alt.ex: Community-based nursing addresses safety, acute, and chronic care needs, enhances self-care capacity, and promotes autonomy in decision making.
w: Making health care decisions on behalf of families
Community-based nursing promotes patients’ autonomy, not decisions made for them.
Limiting care to health promotion without illness care
Community-based nurses provide illness care within the community setting.
Transferring chronic care needs to hospital settings
Community-based nursing includes acute and chronic care in the community.

items: Assess health status
Recognize and analyze cues

items.q: Community-based nursing centers serve as the first level of contact with the health care system. What is a key benefit of providing services near where patients live, work, and socialize?
items.a: It reduces barriers to care and the cost of care for patients
items.ex: Providing care close to home reduces barriers and costs, easing the stress of the financial burden of care.
w: It allows complex surgery to be done outside hospitals
Community centers offer person-centered primary services, not complex surgery.
It removes the need for family involvement in care
These centers include the patient’s family and friends in the plan of care.
It limits services to residents with private insurance
These centers often serve the most underresourced communities.

alt.q: Which communities do community-based nursing centers often serve?
alt.a: The most underresourced communities
alt.ex: Community-based nursing centers often care for the most underresourced communities, offering direct access to nurses.
w: Mainly high-income suburban communities
These centers often serve the most underresourced communities.
Only communities with a nearby trauma center
Centers are the first level of contact, not linked to trauma centers.
Primarily communities needing intensive care
The centers provide comprehensive person-centered services, not intensive care.

items.q: Family-centered care within the community requires a solid knowledge base in which areas? Select all that apply.
o: Family theory
Family theory is part of the knowledge base for family-centered community care.
Principles of communication
Communication principles are required for family-centered care.
Group dynamics
Group dynamics is part of the required knowledge base.
Cultural sensitivity
Cultural sensitivity is required to partner with diverse families.
Advanced hemodynamic monitoring
Hemodynamic monitoring is a critical care skill, not part of this knowledge base.
Hospital accreditation standards
Accreditation standards are not part of the family-centered knowledge base.
items.ex: Family-centered community care requires knowledge of family theory, communication principles, group dynamics, and cultural sensitivity.

alt.q: A nurse partners with a family so they can take responsibility for their health care decisions. Which knowledge supports this family-centered approach? Select all that apply.
o: How families function, based on family theory
Family theory supports family-centered care.
Cultural sensitivity toward the family’s background
Cultural sensitivity is part of the required knowledge base.
Group dynamics among family members
Group dynamics is part of the required knowledge base.
Operating room sterile technique
Sterile technique is not part of family-centered community care knowledge.
Inpatient billing procedures
Billing procedures do not support family-centered partnership.
alt.ex: Correct: How families function, based on family theory; Cultural sensitivity toward the family’s background; Group dynamics among family members.

items.q: A patient tells the community health nurse that she repeatedly has trouble following her prescribed diet. Acting as a counselor, which response by the nurse is best?
items.a: “Let’s talk about what makes following this diet difficult for you.”
items.ex: A counselor first helps patients identify and clarify problems, such as cost of food or unsupportive family, before exploring solutions.
w: “You need to follow this diet exactly as it was prescribed.”
This directs rather than helping the patient identify what blocks success.
“I will plan all of your meals for you this week.”
Counselors do not make decisions for patients; they help patients reach their own.
“Your family should make your food choices from now on.”
This removes the patient’s decision making and skips clarifying the problem.

alt.q: Which statement describes the nurse’s responsibility in the counselor role?
alt.a: Helping patients reach decisions that are best for them
alt.ex: As a counselor, you provide information, listen objectively, and help patients reach their own decisions rather than deciding for them.
w: Making decisions for patients who seem unsure
Counselors do not make decisions; they help patients reach their own.
Giving financial and legal advice to families
Nurses refer for financial or legal issues rather than advising.
Telling patients which solution they must choose
The nurse discusses solutions and supports the patient’s choice.

items.q: Diseases that have newly appeared in a population, or that are rapidly increasing in incidence or geographic range, are called [[emerging infectious diseases|emerging infections|emerging infectious disease|emerging diseases]].
items.ex: Emerging infectious diseases are newly appearing or rapidly increasing in incidence or range; examples include Ebola, Zika, SARS, and COVID-19.

alt.q: Ebola, Zika virus, and COVID-19 are examples of [[emerging infectious diseases|emerging infections|emerging infectious disease|emerging diseases]] that have caused epidemics or pandemics.
alt.ex: Emerging infectious diseases are newly appearing or rapidly increasing in incidence or range; examples include Ebola, Zika, SARS, and COVID-19.

items.q: Which factors have contributed to emerging infections and pandemics? Select all that apply.
o: Increased international travel
International travel spreads infections between regions.
A rise in densely populated urban areas
Crowded urban areas contribute to emerging infections.
Climate change
Climate change is named as a contributor to emerging infections.
Antimicrobial resistance
Emerging infections can also result from antimicrobial resistance.
Wider use of hand hygiene in communities
Hand hygiene is a preventive measure nurses teach, not a cause.
Expanded access to safe vaccines
Equitable vaccine access is a WHO priority for protecting health, not a cause of emergence.
items.ex: International travel, dense urban areas, climate change, and antimicrobial resistance contribute to emerging infections and pandemics.

alt.q: A community health nurse is explaining why new infections such as Zika and COVID-19 have spread worldwide. Which contributing factors should the nurse include? Select all that apply.
o: More people traveling internationally
Increased international travel contributes to emerging infections.
Climate change
Climate change contributes to emerging infections and pandemics.
Growth of crowded urban areas
Densely populated urban areas contribute to emerging infections.
Improved sanitation and clean water
Clean water and sanitation protect health; they are a WHO priority, not a cause.
Greater availability of affordable medications
Affordable medications are a WHO goal, not a cause of emerging infections.
alt.ex: Correct: More people traveling internationally; Climate change; Growth of crowded urban areas.

items.q: Emerging infections cause economic and social disruption because slowing their spread often requires schools, businesses, and public services to close.
items.a: True
items.ex: Closures needed to slow spread, overwhelmed health systems, and supply shortages cause economic and social disruption in communities.
items.ww: The text directly links emerging infections to economic and social disruption, so the statement is accurate.

alt.q: Emerging infections mainly affect a community’s physical health and rarely disrupt its economy or social functions.
alt.a: False
alt.ex: Emerging infections threaten economic and social functions through closures, lost income, supply shortages, and higher costs.
alt.ww: Pandemics cause income loss, isolation, and higher mental health problems, so disruption is common, not rare.

items.q: During a pandemic, which activity reflects a community health nurse’s role described in the textbook?
items.a: Educating the community on hand hygiene and disease prevention
items.ex: During a pandemic, nurses are caregivers, educators on sanitation measures such as hand hygiene, and managers of equipment and supplies.
w: Leaving case investigation entirely to physicians
Community and public health nurses help investigate cases during a crisis.
Limiting care to patients admitted to hospitals
Nurses also provide direct care in the community and through home visits.
Postponing all health teaching until the pandemic ends
Education, including through telehealth, continues during a crisis.

alt.q: Which statement about nurses’ responsibilities during emerging infections and pandemics is accurate?
alt.a: Nurses have an ethical responsibility to care for themselves and their patients
alt.ex: During emerging infections and pandemics, nurses have an ethical responsibility to care for both themselves and their patients.
w: Nurses should set aside their own safety to care for patients
The ethical responsibility includes caring for themselves as well.
Nurses’ role is limited to direct care on hospital units
Nurses also educate, investigate cases, and provide care in the community.
Nurses defer disease detection to public health physicians
Nurses actively participate in preventing and detecting disease.

items.q: Which patient belongs to a medically underserved population?
items.a: A man without a home who sleeps in a shelter
items.ex: People without homes have excess health risks and limited access to care, making them a medically underserved population.
w: An insured teacher who sees her provider every year
Regular insured access to care does not fit the definition.
A young employed adult with a regular health provider
This person has access and no listed excess risk.
A healthy graduate student with campus health coverage
This person has coverage and no listed risk factor or dependence.

alt.q: What defines medically underserved populations?
alt.a: Groups more likely to develop health problems due to excess risks or limited access
alt.ex: Medically underserved groups are more likely to develop health problems because of excess risks, limited access to care, or dependence on others.
w: Groups who choose not to use available health services
The definition centers on risk and access, not personal choice.
Groups with high incomes living in remote vacation areas
Income and vacation homes are not part of the definition.
Groups whose health needs are fully met in outpatient settings
Underserved groups often have needs that are unmet or ignored.

items.q: A nurse is assessing a family from a medically underserved population. Which actions follow the textbook’s assessment guidelines? Select all that apply.
o: Create a comfortable, nonthreatening environment
Setting the stage begins with a comfortable, nonthreatening environment.
Use a professional interpreter if the patient speaks a different language
A professional interpreter supports a culturally competent assessment.
Watch for signs of abuse or neglect, such as being underweight
Nurses stay alert for signs of physical abuse, substance abuse, or neglect.
Consult a social worker if the family needs financial assistance
Financial needs are referred to a social worker.
Give the family legal advice about their housing dispute
Do not give legal advice; provide the patient with a legal resource.
Collect as much home data as possible, even if unrelated to care
Only collect data relevant to providing care to the patient and family.
items.ex: Box 3.1 guides nurses to set a safe tone, use interpreters, watch for abuse, and refer financial or legal issues rather than advise.

alt.q: During a home assessment of a patient from a medically underserved community, which observations are appropriate for the nurse to make? Select all that apply.
o: Whether food is stored properly
Food storage is part of the home assessment.
Signs of insects or vermin
Insects or vermin are listed home assessment observations.
Water stains suggesting a leaky roof
Water stains or a leaky roof are listed observations.
Crime level and busy intersections near the home
The outside environment, including crime and traffic, is assessed.
Value of the family’s furniture and belongings
Only data relevant to care are collected; belongings’ value is not.
Brands of the family’s electronic devices
Device brands are not relevant to providing care.
alt.ex: Correct: Whether food is stored properly; Signs of insects or vermin; Water stains suggesting a leaky roof; Crime level and busy intersections near the home.

items.q: During a home visit, a patient says she is worried about paying rent and has a pending court case. Which action by the nurse is best?
items.a: Consult a social worker and provide her with a legal resource
items.ex: Patients often have financial or legal priorities; the nurse consults a social worker for finances and provides a legal resource.
w: Advise her on how to respond to the court case
Nurses do not provide legal advice themselves.
Tell her to focus on her health care needs first
Patients often have priorities other than health; explore them with her.
Offer to lend her money to cover this month’s rent
Nurses do not provide financial assistance themselves; they consult a social worker.

alt.q: Which statement by a nursing student shows understanding of assessing patients from medically underserved populations?
alt.a: “Patients may have financial or legal priorities ahead of their health.”
alt.ex: Patients often place financial, legal, or social issues ahead of health care, so the nurse explores these issues with them.
w: “I should give legal advice if the patient asks for it.”
Nurses provide a legal resource rather than giving legal advice.
“I can ask the patient’s child to interpret during the visit.”
Guidelines call for a professional interpreter.
“I should judge health beliefs by my own cultural values.”
Nurses do not judge patients’ beliefs by their own culture and values.

items.q: A nurse suspects a patient is being abused by her partner, who stays in the room during the home visit. Which action should the nurse take first?
items.a: Arrange to interview the patient privately without the partner present
items.ex: Interview a patient suspected of being abused in private, when the suspected abuser is not present, because patients may fear retribution.
w: Ask the patient about abuse in front of her partner
Patients may fear retribution if asked in front of the suspected abuser.
Confront the partner about the suspected abuse
Confrontation may endanger the patient and does not protect her.
Document the suspicion and wait until the next visit
Delay does not offer the patient protection or a safe chance to talk.

alt.q: During a private interview, a patient who is being abused says she must have provoked her partner. Which response by the nurse is best?
alt.a: “The abuse is not your fault, and you do not deserve it.”
alt.ex: Use therapeutic communication that reinforces that the abuse is not the victim’s fault.
w: “What did you do that made your partner angry?”
This implies the patient caused the abuse.
“You need to leave your partner today.”
This directs the patient and does not reinforce that she is not at fault.
“Try to avoid arguments so this does not recur.”
This places responsibility for the abuse on the victim.

items.q: Nurses are mandatory reporters of abuse involving adults over age 65, children under age 18, and dependent individuals such as a person with a disability.
items.a: True
items.ex: Nurses must report abuse of elders over 65, children under 18, and dependent individuals.
items.ww: The statement matches all three groups for which nurses are mandatory reporters.

alt.q: A nurse’s duty as a mandatory reporter of abuse applies only to children under age 18.
alt.a: False
alt.ex: Mandatory reporting also covers elders over 65 and dependent individuals, such as a person with a disability.
alt.ww: Children are only one of three groups; elders and dependent individuals are included too.

items.q: A nurse is completing a nursing history for an adolescent mother and her infant. Which action is most appropriate?
items.a: Obtain a nutritional history on both the mother and the baby
items.ex: With an adolescent mother, obtain nutritional histories on both mother and baby while attending to her developmental and social needs.
w: Obtain a nutritional history on the baby only
The mother’s nutrition also needs assessment.
Limit the assessment to the infant’s growth and development
The young mother’s developmental and social needs are also assessed.
Postpone discussing the mother’s social needs until later
The nurse listens to the young mother’s social needs during the history.

alt.q: Why does the nurse identify both developmental and health care needs when taking a family history in an underserved community?
alt.a: To collect enough information to provide family-centered care
alt.ex: The goal of the history is to collect enough information to provide family-centered care.
w: To determine the family’s eligibility for hospital admission
Hospital eligibility is not the purpose of the history.

items.q: A patient who recently immigrated and has diabetes tells the nurse he drinks an herbal tea from his home country to control his blood sugar. Which response by the nurse is best?
items.a: “Tell me more about the tea and what you believe it does for you.”

w: “You should stop the tea and use only your prescribed medicine.”
This judges the practice before learning about it; many such practices complement therapy.
“Herbal remedies are not real treatments for diabetes.”
This dismisses the patient’s beliefs instead of exploring them.
“That is fine; you can skip your medicine when you drink it.”
The nurse must know how the treatment acts before endorsing changes.

alt.q: Immigrant populations often have higher rates of which health conditions?

These conditions are not the ones identified for immigrant populations.
Asthma, eczema, and food allergies
These are not the conditions the text identifies for immigrant populations.
Migraine, gout, and kidney stones
These are not the conditions named for immigrant populations.

items.q: Patients with chronic mental illness are now routinely hospitalized in long-term psychiatric institutions.
items.a: False
items.ex: Patients with chronic mental illness are no longer routinely institutionalized; resources are offered within the community instead.
items.ww: Care has shifted to community resources, so routine long-term institutionalization is not current practice.

alt.q: Many patients with serious mental illness go untreated or undertreated because they have difficulty navigating the health care system.
alt.a: True
alt.ex: Despite community service networks, many patients with serious mental illness go untreated because navigating the system is difficult.
alt.ww: Community networks exist, but navigation problems leave many untreated, so the statement is accurate.

items.q: An older adult who takes several medications tells the community health nurse that he often forgets whether he took his morning doses. Which intervention is most appropriate?
items.a: Teach him to presort doses into small containers labeled with times
items.ex: Presorting uses small containers holding one dose each, labeled with the time to take it.
w: Advise him to take all daily doses together each morning
Combining doses ignores prescribed timing and raises the risk of harm.
Suggest that he stop any medication he cannot remember
Stopping medications without guidance is unsafe.
Have him store all medications together in one large container
Mixing medications in one container increases confusion and error.

alt.q: Which statement by an older adult shows understanding of the presorting technique?
alt.a: “I put each dose in a small container labeled with the time to take it.”
alt.ex: Presorting places one dose in each small container labeled with the specific time to take it.
w: “I keep all my pills in one bottle so they are easy to find.”
Presorting separates individual doses rather than combining pills.
“I take whatever pills I see whenever I remember them.”
Presorting ties each dose to a specific labeled time.
“I put the whole week’s pills together in one bag.”
Presorting uses small containers with one dose each.

items.q: A patient repeatedly misses scheduled visits at the health clinic. Acting as a change agent, which action should the nurse take first?
items.a: Determine why the patient is unable to keep the visits
items.ex: A change agent first finds out why, such as distance or clinic hours, then works with the patient to solve the problem.
w: Discharge the patient from the clinic’s care
This abandons the patient without addressing the cause.
Refer the patient to a different clinic right away
An alternative site is chosen only after learning why visits are missed.
Remind the patient that missed visits harm his health
Reminders do not identify or solve the underlying barrier.

alt.q: A nurse learns that a patient misses clinic visits because the clinic is far away and its hours conflict with her transportation. Which action best reflects the change agent role?
alt.a: Work with the patient to find a closer site with convenient hours
alt.ex: The change agent works with the patient to solve the problem, such as finding a closer nursing clinic with better hours.
w: Tell the patient to arrange different transportation alone
The nurse works with the patient rather than leaving the problem to her.
Document the patient as nonadherent to the plan
Labeling the patient does not solve the access problem.
Advise the patient to use the emergency department instead
Emergency departments are not an appropriate site for routine care.

items.q: Which description best defines community assessment?
items.a: Systematic collection of population data, monitoring of the population’s health status, and sharing information about the community’s health
items.ex: Community assessment gathers population data, tracks the population’s health status, and makes community health information available.
w: A complete head-to-toe physical examination of each resident living within a defined neighborhood
Community assessment focuses on the population and its environment, not on examining every individual.
A survey of patient satisfaction with the hospitals and clinics that serve a particular community
Satisfaction surveys address services, not the population’s health status and environment.
A review of an individual patient’s home for hazards before discharge from an acute care hospital
A home safety check is an individual assessment, which is done against the community background.

alt.q: A nurse is systematically gathering data on a neighborhood’s population, tracking its health status, and publishing findings on its health. What is the nurse performing?
alt.a: A community assessment
alt.ex: Systematic population data collection, health status monitoring, and sharing community health information define community assessment.
w: A family assessment
A family assessment focuses on one family unit, not the whole population of a community.
A focused physical assessment
A focused physical assessment examines one body system of one patient.
A home safety assessment
A home safety assessment examines one patient’s living space, not the community’s population.

items.q: Which three components make up a community, according to the community assessment framework?
items.a: Structure or locale, people, and social systems
items.ex: Each of these three components is examined to identify needs for health policy, health programs, and health services.
w: Housing, income, and transportation
These are all elements of only one component, the structure or locale.
Age, sex, and education level
These are all elements of only one component, the population.
Schools, government, and health care
These are all elements of only one component, the social system.

alt.q: A nursing student is organizing a community assessment. Which grouping should the student use to arrange the data?
alt.a: Structure, population, and social system
alt.ex: Box 3.2 groups community assessment data under structure, population, and social system.
w: Physical, psychological, and spiritual
These are dimensions of an individual’s health, not the components of a community.
Primary, secondary, and tertiary
These are levels of prevention, not the components of a community.
Individual, family, and group
These are types of clients, not the three components of a community.

items.q: How does the nurse gather data about the community’s Structure or locale?
items.a: Travel around the neighborhood and observe its design, services, and meeting places
items.ex: Structure is observed firsthand, demographics come from statistics, and social systems are learned through websites or site visits.
w: Access statistics from reliable websites and the local public health department
That goes with Population.
Visit agency and school websites or schedule a site visit to learn about services
That goes with Social systems.
