items.q: Which complications are classified as collaborative problems because nurses cannot prevent them? Select all that apply.
o: Seizures
Nurses cannot prevent seizures, so they are managed as a collaborative problem.
Hemorrhage
Nurses cannot prevent hemorrhage independently, so it is a collaborative problem.
Pressure injuries
Nurses can prevent pressure injuries, so this is the nursing diagnosis Risk for Pressure Ulcer.
Tracheal aspiration
Nurses can prevent aspiration, so this is the nursing diagnosis Risk for Aspiration.
Swallowing problems
Nurses can treat swallowing problems, so this is the nursing diagnosis Impaired Swallowing.
items.ex: Seizures and hemorrhage are collaborative problems; problems nurses can prevent or treat independently are nursing diagnoses.

alt.q: A nurse sorts a patient’s problems. Which should be labeled as nursing diagnoses rather than collaborative problems? Select all that apply.
o: Risk for Aspiration
Nurses can prevent tracheal aspiration independently, making it a nursing diagnosis.
Impaired Tissue Integrity from a stage 2 pressure injury
Nurses can treat stage 1 or 2 pressure injuries, making this a nursing diagnosis.
Risk for Pressure Ulcer
Nurses can prevent pressure injuries, so this is a nursing diagnosis.
Seizures
Nurses cannot prevent seizures, so this is a collaborative problem.
Hemorrhage
Nurses cannot prevent hemorrhage, so this is a collaborative problem.
alt.ex: Correct: Risk for Aspiration; Impaired Tissue Integrity from a stage 2 pressure injury; Risk for Pressure Ulcer.

items.q: Why is a patient’s risk for pressure injury labeled a nursing diagnosis rather than a collaborative problem?
items.a: Nurses can prevent the onset of pressure injuries independently.
items.ex: When a nurse can independently prevent a complication or provide its primary treatment, the problem is a nursing diagnosis.
w: Pressure injuries require medical treatment as well as nursing care.
Needing medical treatment points toward a collaborative problem, which is not the reason here.
Pressure injuries are identified through diagnostic tests and procedures.
Diagnostic tests are a basis for medical diagnoses, not the reason this is a nursing diagnosis.
Pressure injuries are physiological complications, which are always nursing diagnoses.
Not all physiological complications are nursing diagnoses; seizures and hemorrhage are collaborative problems.

alt.q: A nurse wonders whether to list Risk for Aspiration as a nursing diagnosis or a collaborative problem. Which rule should guide the decision?
alt.a: If the nurse can independently prevent or primarily treat it, it is a nursing diagnosis.
alt.ex: Problems that nurses can prevent or treat on their own are nursing diagnoses; aspiration is one nurses can prevent.
w: If it is a physiological complication, it is always a collaborative problem.
Not all physiological complications are collaborative problems; nurses can prevent aspiration.
If a physician documented it first, it is always a medical diagnosis.
Who documents first does not decide the type; the nurse’s ability to prevent or treat it does.
If it could become serious, it must be a collaborative problem.
Seriousness is not the deciding rule; independent nursing prevention or treatment is.

items.q: Not all physiological complications are collaborative problems.
items.a: True
items.ex: If a nurse can independently prevent or primarily treat a complication, such as aspiration, it is a nursing diagnosis.
items.ww: Calling every physiological complication collaborative ignores problems nurses can prevent or treat on their own.

alt.q: Every physiological complication is a collaborative problem because it involves the patient’s body systems.
alt.a: False
alt.ex: Physiological complications that nurses can prevent or treat independently, such as pressure injuries, are nursing diagnoses.
alt.ww: Some physiological complications, like seizures and hemorrhage, are collaborative, but many others are nursing diagnoses.

items.q: Registered nurses treat patients’ responses to health conditions rather than the medical diagnoses themselves.
items.a: True
items.ex: Nurses cannot treat medical diagnoses; they treat responses such as pain and impaired mobility.
items.ww: Only APRNs among nurses treat medical diagnoses, so registered nurses focus on the patient’s responses.

alt.q: A registered nurse may treat a medical diagnosis such as diabetes mellitus by ordering insulin and an HbA1c test.
alt.a: False
alt.ex: Only APRNs, such as nurse practitioners, can order HbA1c tests or insulin to treat medical diagnoses.
alt.ww: Registered nurses educate about diabetes medication and diet but cannot order its medical treatment.

items.q: Which sources of information does a health care provider use to make a medical diagnosis? Select all that apply.
o: Assessment of physical signs and symptoms
A medical diagnosis is based on a specific assessment of physical signs and symptoms.
The patient’s medical history
The patient’s medical history is one basis for a medical diagnosis.
Results of diagnostic tests and procedures
Diagnostic test and procedure results help confirm a medical diagnosis.
The patient’s response to illness as judged by the nurse
The patient’s response to illness is the basis of a nursing diagnosis.
Nursing interventions already provided to the patient
Interventions follow a diagnosis; they are not the basis for identifying the disease.
items.ex: Medical diagnoses rest on physical signs and symptoms, the medical history, and diagnostic tests and procedures.

alt.q: Which findings would a health care provider use to confirm a medical diagnosis of pneumonia? Select all that apply.
o: Chest x-ray showing infiltrates
Diagnostic imaging results are part of the basis for a medical diagnosis.
Positive blood culture for Pneumococcus
Laboratory test results help the provider confirm the disease condition.
Crackles heard on auscultation
Physical signs such as abnormal lung sounds support a medical diagnosis.
The nurse’s judgment of the patient’s coping response
A judgment about the patient’s response forms a nursing diagnosis, not a medical one.
The nursing care plan for the patient
The care plan is built after diagnoses are made; it does not confirm the disease.
alt.ex: Correct: Chest x-ray showing infiltrates; Positive blood culture for Pneumococcus; Crackles heard on auscultation.

items.q: Which of the following is a nursing diagnosis rather than a medical diagnosis?
items.a: Impaired Respiratory System Function
items.ex: Impaired Respiratory System Function names the patient’s response to illness; pneumonia names the disease itself.
w: Community-acquired pneumonia
Pneumonia is a disease condition, so it is a medical diagnosis.
Rheumatoid arthritis of the hands
Rheumatoid arthritis is a disease condition treated by physicians and APRNs.
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Diabetes mellitus is a medical diagnosis managed with provider-ordered medications and tests.

alt.q: Which of the following is a medical diagnosis rather than a nursing diagnosis?
alt.a: Leukemia
alt.ex: Leukemia is a disease condition, which makes it a medical diagnosis treated by physicians and APRNs.
w: Acute Pain
Acute Pain is a nursing diagnosis describing a patient’s response to a health condition.
Anxiety
Anxiety is a nursing diagnosis that nurses are licensed to treat independently.
Self-Care Deficit
Self-care deficit is a nursing diagnosis, not a disease condition.

items.q: A patient is breathing rapidly. One nurse labels the problem “anger,” and another labels it “impaired breathing.” What does this example show about diagnostic labels?
items.a: Each label prompts nurses to consider very different causes for the problem.
items.ex: Anger points to emotional or behavioral causes, while impaired breathing points to respiratory causes, so clear standard labels matter.
w: Either label leads the team to the same interventions for the patient.
The labels point to different causes and therefore different care, so they are not interchangeable.
The choice of label matters little once the medical diagnosis is known.
Clear labels familiar to all providers are needed to understand and manage the patient’s needs.
Labels are most useful when each nurse chooses personal wording.
Personal wording causes inconsistency; standardized terminology gives diagnostic clarity.

alt.q: Why does the textbook stress using a clear, standardized label when making a diagnosis?
alt.a: So all members of the health care team understand the patient’s problems and communicate effectively
alt.ex: Standardized terminology provides diagnostic clarity so the whole team understands the problem and can communicate about it.
w: So the nurse can avoid assessing the cause of the patient’s problem
A clear label prompts nurses to consider causes; it does not replace assessment.
So nursing diagnoses can be replaced by the patient’s medical diagnoses
Nursing and medical diagnoses are different types; one does not replace the other.
So each nurse can describe problems in words most familiar to them
Personal wording works against clarity; a label familiar to all providers is needed.

items.q: A nurse assesses a patient who has a stage 2 pressure injury on the sacrum. How should the nurse classify this problem?
items.a: As the nursing diagnosis Impaired Tissue Integrity
items.ex: Nurses can treat stage 1 or 2 pressure injuries, so the problem is the nursing diagnosis Impaired Tissue Integrity.
w: As a collaborative problem requiring medical treatment
Collaborative problems are those nurses cannot prevent; nurses can treat stage 1 or 2 pressure injuries.
As a medical diagnosis that only an APRN may treat
Stage 1 or 2 pressure injuries are within the nurse’s independent treatment.
As the nursing diagnosis Risk for Pressure Ulcer
The injury already exists, so it is no longer only a risk.

alt.q: A patient has difficulty swallowing after a stroke, and the nurse can provide the primary treatment. How is this problem classified?
alt.a: As the nursing diagnosis Impaired Swallowing
alt.ex: When nurses can treat a problem such as swallowing difficulty, it is labeled as a nursing diagnosis.
w: As a collaborative problem the nurse only monitors
Collaborative problems are those nurses cannot prevent or primarily treat.
As a medical diagnosis treated only by the provider
Swallowing problems are listed among problems nurses can treat independently.
As the nursing diagnosis Risk for Aspiration
The swallowing problem already exists; Risk for Aspiration names a problem nurses prevent.

items.q: A postoperative patient may develop hemorrhage. Which statement best describes the nurse’s role in managing this problem?
items.a: Monitor the patient’s condition and work with the provider to prevent the complication.
items.ex: Hemorrhage is a collaborative problem nurses cannot prevent alone, so nursing focuses on monitoring and prevention alongside provider orders.
w: Treat the hemorrhage independently using only nursing-prescribed interventions.
Collaborative problems require provider-prescribed interventions in addition to nursing care.
Write the nursing diagnosis Risk for Hemorrhage and manage it alone.
Nurses cannot prevent hemorrhage independently, so it is a collaborative problem, not a nursing diagnosis.
Leave all care for this problem to the surgeon because it is medical.
Nurses play an active role by monitoring and helping prevent the complication.

alt.q: A patient with a brain tumor is at risk for seizures. How should the nurse categorize and approach this problem?
alt.a: As a collaborative problem that the nurse monitors while carrying out prescribed interventions
alt.ex: Seizures cannot be prevented by nurses alone, so they are a collaborative problem managed with both nursing and provider interventions.
w: As a nursing diagnosis that the nurse can prevent with independent care
Nurses cannot prevent seizures independently, so this is not a nursing diagnosis.
As a medical diagnosis that requires no nursing involvement
Collaborative problems involve nurses, who monitor and help prevent complications.
As a health promotion diagnosis focused on behavior change
Health promotion diagnoses describe a desire to improve health, not a potential complication.

items.q: [[Collaborative problems|Collaborative problem]] are potential problems that nurses manage using both independent and health care provider–prescribed interventions.
items.ex: These problems need both medical and nursing interventions, with nursing focused on monitoring and prevention.

alt.q: Seizures and hemorrhage, which nurses cannot prevent on their own, are examples of [[collaborative problems|collaborative problem]].
alt.ex: These problems need both medical and nursing interventions, with nursing focused on monitoring and prevention.

items.q: Which outcomes does interprofessional collaboration produce? Select all that apply.
o: Involves patients and families in decision making about their care
Collaboration ensures patients and families take part in care decisions.
Improves coordination between different disciplines
Communication among disciplines improves coordination of care.
Improves access to health interventions
Interprofessional collaboration improves patients’ access to health interventions.
Enhances the delivery of person-centered care
Team collaboration enhances person-centered care and improves outcomes.
Allows each discipline to plan care without input from the others
Collaboration depends on considering one another’s unique perspectives, not planning in isolation.
Removes the need for the nurse to monitor collaborative problems
Nurses still monitor collaborative problems; collaboration adds to that role.
items.ex: When disciplines and patients share perspectives, care is more person-centered, coordinated, and accessible, with patients and families involved.

alt.q: A nurse explains to a student why interprofessional collaboration matters. Which statements should the nurse include? Select all that apply.
o: It improves patient and health system outcomes.
Collaboration improves patient and health systems outcomes.
It helps the team manage the many factors that influence health.
Sharing perspectives helps manage the many factors affecting health.
It involves the patient and family in care decisions.
Collaboration ensures patients and families take part in decision making.
It lets the nurse treat medical diagnoses without a provider.
Registered nurses cannot treat medical diagnoses, even within a team.
It means one discipline makes decisions for the whole team.
Collaboration relies on each discipline’s perspective, not a single decision maker.
alt.ex: Correct: It improves patient and health system outcomes; It helps the team manage the many factors that influence health; It involves the patient and family in care decisions.

items.q: A nursing diagnosis can describe the response of a family or a community, not only an individual patient.
items.a: True
items.ex: A nursing diagnosis classifies an individual’s, family’s, or community’s response to illness.
items.ww: Limiting nursing diagnoses to individuals ignores that nurses treat family, group, and community responses.

alt.q: A nursing diagnosis applies only to an individual patient and cannot describe the response of a family or community.
alt.a: False
alt.ex: Nursing diagnoses classify individual, family, or community responses, and nurses treat patient and group responses.
alt.ww: Families and communities also have responses to illness that nurses identify and treat.

items.q: Why are nursing diagnoses such as Acute Pain or Activity Intolerance useful in patient care?
items.a: They give clear direction about the nursing interventions nurses may provide independently.
items.ex: Nursing diagnoses point directly to the independent interventions nurses are licensed to provide.
w: They identify the disease that the health care provider must treat.
Identifying the disease is the purpose of a medical diagnosis.
They authorize the nurse to order medications for the patient.
Registered nurses cannot order medications to treat medical conditions.
They replace the need for the patient’s medical diagnosis.
Nursing and medical diagnoses serve different purposes and are both needed.

alt.q: A nurse records Activity Intolerance for a patient with heart failure. What is the main benefit of this nursing diagnosis?
alt.a: It guides the nurse to independent interventions for the patient’s response.
alt.ex: A nursing diagnosis directs the type of independent nursing interventions to address the patient’s response.
w: It confirms the disease process causing the patient’s fatigue.
Confirming a disease process is the role of the medical diagnosis.
It allows the nurse to prescribe heart failure medications.
Prescribing medications for disease is outside the registered nurse’s scope.
It makes the heart failure a collaborative problem instead.
The nursing diagnosis does not change the classification of the medical condition.

items.q: Which organization developed the International Classification for Nursing Practice (ICNP)?
items.a: The International Council of Nurses (ICN)
items.ex: The ICN, a federation of national nurses’ associations, developed the ICNP to represent diagnoses, interventions, and outcomes.
w: The World Health Organization (WHO)
WHO accepts the ICNP as part of health services but did not develop it.
NANDA International (NANDA-I)
NANDA-I maintains its own separate nursing diagnosis classification system.
The American Nurses Association (ANA)
The ANA recognizes standard terminologies, but the ICN developed the ICNP.

alt.q: The International Council of Nurses (ICN) developed which standardized terminology that is used throughout this textbook?
alt.a: International Classification for Nursing Practice (ICNP)
alt.ex: The ICN developed the ICNP, the terminology used throughout the text and increasingly in hospitals.
w: Clinical Care Classification (CCC) System
The CCC is another ANA-recognized terminology, not the ICN’s classification.
Nursing Interventions Classification (NIC)
NIC classifies interventions and is not the ICN’s terminology.
Perioperative Nursing Data Set (PNDS)
PNDS is a perioperative terminology, not the ICN’s classification.

items.q: What does the ICNP axis Focus describe?
items.a: The area of attention that is relevant to nursing
items.ex: The ICNP’s multiaxial model lets nurses combine terms such as focus and judgment to build a diagnostic concept.
w: Clinical opinion or determination related to the focus
That goes with Judgment.
Subject to whom a diagnosis refers and who receives an intervention
That goes with Client.
An intentional process applied to or performed by a client
That goes with Action.

alt.q: What does the ICNP axis Judgment describe?
alt.a: Clinical opinion or determination related to the focus
alt.ex: The ICNP’s multiaxial model lets nurses combine terms such as focus and judgment to build a diagnostic concept.
w: The area of attention that is relevant to nursing
That goes with Focus.
Subject to whom a diagnosis refers and who receives an intervention
That goes with Client.
An intentional process applied to or performed by a client
That goes with Action.

alt.q: What does the ICNP axis Client describe?
alt.a: Subject to whom a diagnosis refers and who receives an intervention
alt.ex: The ICNP’s multiaxial model lets nurses combine terms such as focus and judgment to build a diagnostic concept.
w: The area of attention that is relevant to nursing
That goes with Focus.
Clinical opinion or determination related to the focus
That goes with Judgment.
An intentional process applied to or performed by a client
That goes with Action.

alt.q: What does the ICNP axis Action describe?
alt.a: An intentional process applied to or performed by a client
alt.ex: The ICNP’s multiaxial model lets nurses combine terms such as focus and judgment to build a diagnostic concept.
w: The area of attention that is relevant to nursing
That goes with Focus.
Clinical opinion or determination related to the focus
That goes with Judgment.
Subject to whom a diagnosis refers and who receives an intervention
That goes with Client.

alt.q: What does the ICNP axis Means describe?
alt.a: A manner or method of accomplishing an intervention
alt.ex: The ICNP’s multiaxial model lets nurses combine terms such as focus and judgment to build a diagnostic concept.
w: The area of attention that is relevant to nursing
That goes with Focus.
Clinical opinion or determination related to the focus
That goes with Judgment.
Subject to whom a diagnosis refers and who receives an intervention
That goes with Client.

alt.q: What does the ICNP axis Location describe?
alt.a: Anatomical and spatial orientation of a diagnosis or intervention
alt.ex: The ICNP’s multiaxial model lets nurses combine terms such as focus and judgment to build a diagnostic concept.
w: The area of attention that is relevant to nursing
That goes with Focus.
Clinical opinion or determination related to the focus
That goes with Judgment.
Subject to whom a diagnosis refers and who receives an intervention
That goes with Client.

alt.q: Which ICNP axis is “The area of attention that is relevant to nursing”?
alt.a: Focus
alt.ex: The ICNP’s multiaxial model lets nurses combine terms such as focus and judgment to build a diagnostic concept.
w: Judgment
Judgment: Clinical opinion or determination related to the focus.
Client
Client: Subject to whom a diagnosis refers and who receives an intervention.
Action
Action: An intentional process applied to or performed by a client.

alt.q: Which ICNP axis is “Clinical opinion or determination related to the focus”?
alt.a: Judgment
alt.ex: The ICNP’s multiaxial model lets nurses combine terms such as focus and judgment to build a diagnostic concept.
w: Focus
Focus: The area of attention that is relevant to nursing.
Client
Client: Subject to whom a diagnosis refers and who receives an intervention.
Action
Action: An intentional process applied to or performed by a client.

alt.q: Which ICNP axis is “Subject to whom a diagnosis refers and who receives an intervention”?
alt.a: Client
alt.ex: The ICNP’s multiaxial model lets nurses combine terms such as focus and judgment to build a diagnostic concept.
w: Focus
Focus: The area of attention that is relevant to nursing.
Judgment
Judgment: Clinical opinion or determination related to the focus.
Action
Action: An intentional process applied to or performed by a client.

alt.q: Which ICNP axis is “An intentional process applied to or performed by a client”?
alt.a: Action
alt.ex: The ICNP’s multiaxial model lets nurses combine terms such as focus and judgment to build a diagnostic concept.
w: Focus
Focus: The area of attention that is relevant to nursing.
Judgment
Judgment: Clinical opinion or determination related to the focus.
Client
Client: Subject to whom a diagnosis refers and who receives an intervention.

alt.q: Which ICNP axis is “A manner or method of accomplishing an intervention”?
alt.a: Means
alt.ex: The ICNP’s multiaxial model lets nurses combine terms such as focus and judgment to build a diagnostic concept.
w: Focus
Focus: The area of attention that is relevant to nursing.
Judgment
Judgment: Clinical opinion or determination related to the focus.
Client
Client: Subject to whom a diagnosis refers and who receives an intervention.

alt.q: Which ICNP axis is “Anatomical and spatial orientation of a diagnosis or intervention”?
alt.a: Location
alt.ex: The ICNP’s multiaxial model lets nurses combine terms such as focus and judgment to build a diagnostic concept.
w: Focus
Focus: The area of attention that is relevant to nursing.
Judgment
Judgment: Clinical opinion or determination related to the focus.
Client
Client: Subject to whom a diagnosis refers and who receives an intervention.

mt.q: Match each ICNP axis with its definition.
pairs: The area of attention that is relevant to nursing
Clinical opinion or determination related to the focus
Subject to whom a diagnosis refers and who receives an intervention
An intentional process applied to or performed by a client
A manner or method of accomplishing an intervention
Anatomical and spatial orientation of a diagnosis or intervention
mt.ex: The ICNP’s multiaxial model lets nurses combine terms such as focus and judgment to build a diagnostic concept.

items.q: A nurse combines the ICNP term “pain” with the term “chronic” to create the diagnosis Chronic Pain. From which axis does “chronic” come?
items.a: Duration
items.ex: The book's example combines “pain” from the Focus axis with “chronic” from the ICNP Duration axis.
w: Judgment
Judgment terms are clinical opinions such as risk, enhanced, or decreasing level.
Focus
“Pain” is the Focus term in this diagnosis; “chronic” describes its duration.
Location
Location terms describe anatomical or spatial orientation, such as abdomen or school.

alt.q: In the ICNP diagnosis Chronic Pain, which axis supplies the term “pain”?
alt.a: Focus
alt.ex: Pain is an area of attention relevant to nursing, so it comes from the Focus axis; “chronic” comes from the Duration axis.
w: Duration
The Duration axis supplies “chronic,” not “pain.”
Judgment
Judgment terms are clinical opinions such as risk or enhanced.
Client
Client terms name the recipient, such as patient, family, or community.

items.q: Which term is an example from the ICNP Judgment axis?
items.a: Enhanced
items.ex: Judgment terms are clinical opinions about the focus, such as decreasing level, risk, enhanced, interrupted, or abnormal.
w: Caregiver
Caregiver is a Client axis term naming the recipient of care.
Abdomen
Abdomen is a Location axis term describing anatomical orientation.
Monitoring
Monitoring is an Action axis term describing an intentional process.

alt.q: In the ICNP, the term “risk” belongs to which axis?
alt.a: Judgment
alt.ex: Risk is a clinical opinion about the focus of nursing practice, which places it on the Judgment axis.
w: Focus
Focus terms are areas of attention such as pain, elimination, or knowledge.
Action
Action terms are intentional processes such as educating or administering.
Means
Means terms are methods of accomplishing an intervention, such as a bandage.

items.q: A community health nurse identifies a health problem that affects an entire neighborhood. In the ICNP, the term “community” comes from which axis?
items.a: Client
items.ex: The Client axis names the subject of the diagnosis and recipient of intervention, such as a newborn, family, or community.
w: Location
Location includes places like a community health center, but the recipient of care is a Client term.
Focus
Focus terms name the area of nursing attention, such as homelessness or pain.
Judgment
Judgment terms are clinical opinions such as risk or abnormal.

alt.q: Which set of terms all belong to the ICNP Client axis?
alt.a: Newborn, caregiver, family, community
alt.ex: Client terms name to whom a diagnosis refers and who receives the intervention.
w: Educating, changing, administering, monitoring
These are Action axis terms describing intentional processes.
Posterior, abdomen, school, community health center
These are Location axis terms describing anatomical or spatial orientation.
Pain, homelessness, elimination, knowledge
These are Focus axis terms describing areas of nursing attention.

items.q: A nurse documents an intervention: “Educating caregiver about bladder-training technique.” In the ICNP, “bladder-training technique” comes from which axis?
items.a: Means
items.ex: Means is the manner or method of accomplishing an intervention, such as a bandage or bladder-training technique.
w: Action
“Educating” is the Action term; the technique is the method used.
Client
“Caregiver” is the Client term, the recipient of the intervention.
Focus
Focus terms name areas of nursing attention, not the method of an intervention.

alt.q: In the ICNP intervention “Educating caregiver about bladder-training technique,” from which axis does the term “educating” come?
alt.a: Action
alt.ex: Action terms are intentional processes applied to or performed by a client, such as educating or monitoring.
w: Means
Means supplies “bladder-training technique,” the method used to accomplish the intervention.
Client
Client supplies “caregiver,” the recipient of the intervention.
Judgment
Judgment terms are clinical opinions such as risk or enhanced, not processes.

items.q: Which are ANA-recognized standard nursing terminologies? Select all that apply.
o: Omaha System
The Omaha System is listed among the ANA-recognized terminologies.
Clinical Care Classification (CCC) System
The CCC System is an ANA-recognized interface terminology.
Perioperative Nursing Data Set (PNDS)
PNDS is listed among the ANA-recognized terminologies.
Nursing Outcomes Classification (NOC)
NOC is an ANA-recognized terminology for outcomes.
International Classification of Diseases (ICD)
ICD classifies diseases for medical diagnosis and is not listed as a nursing terminology.
Diagnostic and Statistical Manual (DSM)
The DSM is not among the ANA-recognized standard nursing terminologies.
items.ex: ANA-recognized terminologies include CCC, ICNP, NANDA-I, NIC, NOC, Omaha System, PNDS, and ABC Codes.

alt.q: A nurse is reviewing terminologies built into the agency’s electronic health record. Which are ANA-recognized standard nursing terminologies? Select all that apply.
o: NANDA International (NANDA-I)
NANDA-I is one of the ANA-recognized standard nursing terminologies.
Nursing Interventions Classification (NIC)
NIC is an ANA-recognized terminology for nursing interventions.
International Classification for Nursing Practice (ICNP)
The ICNP is ANA-recognized and used throughout this text.
International Classification of Diseases (ICD)
ICD classifies diseases and is not listed among nursing terminologies.
Current Procedural Terminology (CPT)
CPT is not listed among the ANA-recognized standard nursing terminologies.
alt.ex: Correct: NANDA International (NANDA-I); Nursing Interventions Classification (NIC); International Classification for Nursing Practice (ICNP).

items.q: For what purpose did the International Council of Nurses develop the ICNP?
items.a: To support standardized nursing documentation at the point of care
items.ex: The ICNP is a unified nursing language system that supports standardized documentation at the bedside or point of care.
w: To classify diseases for physician billing and reimbursement
Classifying diseases describes medical diagnosis, not the purpose of a nursing terminology.
To replace all other nursing terminologies in every country
Several standard terminologies remain in use; the ICNP adapts to many purposes.
To list the medications nurses may order independently
The ICNP represents diagnoses, interventions, and outcomes, not prescribing authority.

alt.q: A nurse documents at the bedside using ICNP terms. Which feature of the ICNP supports this use?
alt.a: It is a unified nursing language designed for point-of-care documentation.
alt.ex: The ICNP was built as a unified language to support standardized nursing documentation at the bedside.
w: It is a disease classification designed for physician documentation.
The ICNP is a nursing terminology, not a disease classification for physicians.
It is a list of interventions that can only be used in research.
The ICNP adapts to documentation, research, and practice guidelines.
It is a system used only in North American hospitals.
The ICNP is an international terminology used in different countries.

items.q: The World Health Organization accepts the ICNP as including nursing practice as an essential and complementary part of professional health services.
items.a: True
items.ex: WHO accepts the ICNP to include the nursing domain as an essential, complementary part of health services.
items.ww: WHO did accept the ICNP; its role is acceptance rather than development of the terminology.

alt.q: The World Health Organization developed the ICNP as a unified nursing language system.
alt.a: False
alt.ex: The International Council of Nurses developed the ICNP; WHO accepts it.
alt.ww: WHO accepts the ICNP, but the ICN, not WHO, created it.

items.q: What did the formation of the North American Nursing Diagnosis Association (NANDA) classification system allow?
items.a: Diagnosis to become a step in the five-step nursing process
items.ex: The NANDA classification allowed diagnosis to become a step in the five-step nursing process.
w: Nurses to order diagnostic tests for medical conditions
Ordering diagnostic tests for disease remains the role of physicians and APRNs.
Medical diagnoses to be written within nursing statements
Medical diagnoses should not be included in nursing diagnostic statements.
The ICNP axes to be combined into a single classification
NANDA-I and ICNP are separate systems with many shared and differing labels.

alt.q: Which development made diagnosis a formal step in the five-step nursing process?
alt.a: Formation of the NANDA nursing diagnosis classification system
alt.ex: Formation of NANDA’s classification system allowed diagnosis to become a step in the nursing process.
w: Acceptance of the ICNP by the World Health Organization
WHO acceptance recognized nursing’s domain; it did not create the diagnosis step.
Recognition of the Omaha System by the ANA
ANA recognition of terminologies did not create the diagnosis step.
Adoption of nursing diagnoses in electronic health records
EHR use came later and did not add diagnosis to the nursing process.

items.q: Which are aims of the NANDA-I system? Select all that apply.
o: Name actual or potential human responses to health problems
NANDA-I aims to name actual or potential human responses.
Develop and disseminate evidence-based terminology for nurses’ clinical judgments
NANDA-I develops and spreads evidence-based terminology.
Document care for the reimbursement of nursing services
Documenting care for reimbursement is one of NANDA-I’s aims.
Contribute to informatics and information standards
NANDA-I contributes to developing informatics and information standards.
Name disease conditions for physicians to treat
Naming diseases is the purpose of medical diagnosis, not NANDA-I.
Replace the ICNP in all clinical settings
NANDA-I and the ICNP coexist and are used in different settings.
items.ex: NANDA-I names human responses, spreads evidence-based terminology, supports reimbursement documentation, and contributes to informatics standards.

alt.q: A nurse educator describes the work of NANDA International today. Which statements are accurate? Select all that apply.
o: It reviews nursing diagnoses and their classification.
NANDA-I continues to review nursing diagnoses and their classification.
It provides definitions and defining characteristics for diagnoses.
NANDA-I provides formal statements with definitions and defining characteristics.
It provides related or risk factors for diagnoses.
NANDA-I diagnostic statements include related or risk factors.
It was developed by the International Council of Nurses.
The ICN developed the ICNP, not NANDA-I.
It is used to order medications for nursing diagnoses.
NANDA-I is a diagnostic terminology and does not authorize prescribing.
alt.ex: Correct: It reviews nursing diagnoses and their classification; It provides definitions and defining characteristics for diagnoses; It provides related or risk factors for diagnoses.

items.q: What does NANDA-I provide for each standard, formal diagnostic statement?
items.a: A definition, defining characteristics, and related or risk factors
items.ex: NANDA-I provides formal diagnostic statements that include definitions, defining characteristics, and related or risk factors.
w: A medical diagnosis, prescribed treatment, and expected cure
These belong to medical diagnosis and treatment, not NANDA-I statements.
A focus, judgment, and client term from separate axes
Combining axis terms describes how ICNP diagnoses are built.
A nursing intervention, outcome, and evaluation date
Interventions and outcomes are planned after the diagnosis and are not part of its statement.

alt.q: A nurse looks up a NANDA-I diagnosis to confirm it fits the patient. Which information will the nurse find with the diagnosis?
alt.a: Its definition, defining characteristics, and related or risk factors
alt.ex: NANDA-I supplies definitions, defining characteristics, and related or risk factors for comparing with patient data.
w: Its matching medical diagnosis and prescribed medications
NANDA-I describes nursing responses, not medical diagnoses or prescriptions.
Its required terms from the Focus and Judgment axes
Focus and Judgment axes belong to the ICNP model.
Its list of interventions the provider must approve
NANDA-I diagnoses do not include provider-approved intervention lists.

items.q: How does the language of the ICNP differ from that of NANDA-I?
items.a: The ICNP refers to nursing diagnoses, while NANDA-I officially refers to diagnostic labels.
items.ex: The two systems differ in wording: the ICNP uses “nursing diagnoses,” and NANDA-I officially uses “diagnostic labels.”
w: The ICNP refers to diagnostic labels, while NANDA-I officially refers to nursing diagnoses.
This reverses the terms each system officially uses.
The ICNP refers to medical diagnoses, while NANDA-I officially refers to collaborative problems.
Neither system names medical diagnoses or collaborative problems as its terms.
The ICNP refers to defining characteristics, while NANDA-I officially refers to axes.
Axes belong to the ICNP model, and defining characteristics are a NANDA-I element.

alt.q: Which term does NANDA-I officially use for the diagnoses in its classification?
alt.a: Diagnostic labels
alt.ex: NANDA-I officially refers to diagnostic labels, whereas the ICNP taxonomy refers to nursing diagnoses.
w: Nursing diagnoses
The ICNP taxonomy is the one that refers to nursing diagnoses.
Focus terms
Focus is an ICNP axis, not NANDA-I’s official term.
Collaborative problems
Collaborative problems are a separate type of problem, not NANDA-I’s term.

items.q: NANDA-I and the ICNP share many labels for certain diagnoses but also use different labels for many similar responses.
items.a: True
items.ex: The systems overlap in many labels yet vary in many labels describing similar responses to health conditions.
items.ww: The two systems are similar in language, but they are not identical; many labels differ.

alt.q: NANDA-I and the ICNP use identical labels for every nursing diagnosis, so the systems are interchangeable.
alt.a: False
alt.ex: Although they share many labels, the two systems vary in many labels for similar responses.
alt.ww: Many labels do match, but many others differ, so the systems are not interchangeable.

items.q: Two nurses on the same unit describe one patient’s problem in different, unspecific words in the health record. What is the main concern with this practice?
items.a: It causes inconsistency in naming the patient’s needs, interventions, and expected outcomes.
items.ex: Unspecific, unclear wording causes inconsistencies in naming nursing diagnoses, interventions, and expected treatment outcomes.
w: It slows documentation but has little effect on patient care.
Inconsistent naming affects communication and quality of care, not just speed.
It is acceptable as long as the medical diagnosis is recorded.
The medical diagnosis does not convey nursing problems; nursing needs a standardized language.
It is preferred because personal wording is more individualized.
Individualized care comes from accurate data, not from nonstandard wording.

alt.q: A nurse manager encourages staff to use standardized nursing terminology. Which explanation best supports this request?
alt.a: A common language communicates patient problems clearly across disciplines and care settings.
alt.ex: Standard terminology lets nurses communicate patient problems meaningfully across all disciplines and settings.
w: A common language reduces the need for nurses to assess patients.
Standard terms describe assessment findings; they do not replace assessment.
A common language lets nurses treat medical diagnoses independently.
Standard terminology does not change the registered nurse’s scope of practice.
A common language is required only for billing, not patient care.
Standard language improves communication, care quality, and knowledge, not just billing.

items.q: A nurse attends a discharge planning conference with a physical therapist and a social worker for a 73-year-old patient who fell and has limited exercise tolerance. Which action by the nurse best supports interprofessional collaboration?
items.a: Share standardized nursing diagnoses with their supporting assessment findings.
items.ex: Standard terms with agreed-upon definitions let all disciplines understand the patient’s problems the same way.
w: Describe the patient’s problems in the nurse’s own informal wording.
Unspecific wording causes inconsistencies and confusion across disciplines.
Report only the medical diagnoses because other disciplines know them.
Medical diagnoses do not describe the patient’s responses that nursing addresses.
Let the other disciplines set the plan without nursing input.
Collaboration depends on each discipline sharing its unique perspective.

alt.q: During an interprofessional meeting, a nurse wants to communicate a patient’s fall risk clearly. Which approach is best?
alt.a: Use the standardized diagnosis Risk for Fall with its supporting findings.
alt.ex: A standardized diagnosis with findings gives every discipline the same clear understanding of the problem.
w: Say the patient seems “a bit unsteady” without further detail.
Vague wording leads to inconsistent understanding of the patient’s needs.
State only the patient’s cardiac and respiratory diagnoses.
Medical diagnoses do not convey the patient’s nursing problem of fall risk.
Wait for the therapist to describe the problem first.
The nurse contributes a nursing perspective that should be shared clearly.

items.q: For which purposes do nurses and hospital staff use data-based information from the ICNP? Select all that apply.
o: Planning and managing nursing care
ICNP data support planning and managing nursing care.
Financial forecasting
ICNP data are used for financial forecasting.
Analysis of patient outcomes
ICNP data support analysis of patient outcomes.
Health policy development
ICNP data contribute to health policy development.
Confirming medical diagnoses
Medical diagnoses are confirmed by providers using signs, history, and tests.
Prescribing medical treatments
Prescribing medical treatment is outside the purpose of a nursing terminology.
items.ex: ICNP data are used for planning and managing care, financial forecasting, outcome analysis, and health policy development.

alt.q: A hospital wants to use ICNP-coded nursing data. Which uses are supported by the textbook? Select all that apply.
o: Developing health policy
ICNP data contribute to health policy development.
Analyzing patient outcomes
ICNP data support analysis of patient outcomes.
Forecasting finances
ICNP data are used in financial forecasting.
Ordering laboratory tests
Ordering tests is a provider function, not a use of ICNP data.
Diagnosing diseases
Diagnosing disease is the purpose of medical diagnosis, not the ICNP.
alt.ex: Correct: Developing health policy; Analyzing patient outcomes; Forecasting finances.

items.q: [[Standard terminologies|Standardized terminologies|standard terminology]] are a collection of terms used in the clinical assessment, management, and care of patients.
items.ex: Standard terminologies include agreed-upon definitions that represent the knowledge behind the terms.

alt.q: A collection of terms with agreed-upon definitions used in assessing, managing, and caring for patients is called a [[standard terminology|standardized terminology]].
alt.ex: Standard terminologies include agreed-upon definitions that represent the knowledge behind the terms.

items.q: In addition to improving communication, what does standard nursing terminology create for the profession?
items.a: A scientific knowledge base for nursing
items.ex: Standard terminology creates a scientific knowledge base that connects nursing theory, research, and practice.
w: A legal authority to treat medical diagnoses
Terminology does not change scope; registered nurses still cannot treat medical diagnoses.
A replacement for the nursing assessment
Standard terms describe assessment data; they do not replace assessment.
A single labeling system used worldwide
Several terminologies remain in use, and their labels often differ.

alt.q: How does standard terminology such as nursing diagnosis help advance the discipline of nursing?
alt.a: It connects theory, research, and nursing practice.
alt.ex: Standard terms support documentation and evidence-based guidelines, linking theory, research, and practice to generate knowledge.
w: It removes the need for evidence-based guidelines.
Standard terminology facilitates the use of evidence-based clinical guidelines.
It limits nursing to documenting medical orders.
Standard terminology names nursing’s own judgments and interventions.
It separates nursing research from clinical care.
Standard terms connect research with practice rather than separating them.

items.q: The multiaxial ICNP model allows nurses to combine terms from different axes to create a diagnostic concept.
items.a: True
items.ex: Terms such as “pain” (Focus) and “chronic” (Duration axis) can be combined to form the diagnosis “chronic pain.”
items.ww: The ICNP is designed for combining terms; a single axis alone rarely forms a complete diagnosis.

alt.q: Each ICNP diagnosis is a fixed label taken from a single axis, and terms from different axes are never combined.
alt.a: False
alt.ex: The ICNP’s seven axes are designed so nurses combine terms, such as Focus and Time, into diagnoses.
alt.ww: Combining axis terms is the core feature of the multiaxial ICNP model.
